articles.title: Eagles Updated Draft Capital Following The Jordan Davis Trade
articles.summary: Here is a breakdown of the Philadelphia Eagles' updated draft capital over the next three drafts following the Jordan Davis trade.
articles.body: By shipping defensive tackle Jordan Davis to Jacksonville for a massive return, Philadelphia Eagles general manager Howie Roseman has once again armed himself with premium future draft capital. First it was A.J. Brown to New England for a 2028 first-round pick and a 2027 fifth-rounder, now Davis to the Jaguars for a 2027 first and 2029 second round pick. Roseman is stockpiling draft assets and with the Eagles sitting at 2-7, it's clear the Eagles could be pivoting toward a potential rebuild. It wasn't just Brown and Davis. Roseman also shipped center Cam Jurgens to Baltimore for a 2028 second-round pick and a 2027 fifth-rounder. The Eagles are building a war chest of draft assets and with the NFL Trade Deadline fast approaching, more moves could be on the way. Some potential names on the move could include running back Saquon Barkley, tight end Dallas Goedert and wide receiver Marquise Brown. Even if Tuesday’s Trade Deadline passes without another move, the groundwork is already laid out. Armed with a treasure trove of future picks through the 2029 draft, Roseman has given the Eagles a major jump-start on their impending roster reset Here is a breakdown of the Eagles' updated draft capital over the next three drafts following the Davis trade, per Spotrac: 2027 NFL Draft Round 1: Own, Jaguars (Jordan Davis trade) Round 2: Own Round 3: Projected Compensatory Pick (Jaelan Phillips free agent departure) Round 4: Own Round 5: Own, Ravens (Jurgens trade), Patriots (Brown trade) Round 6: None Round 7: Minnesota Vikings (Sam Howell trade) 2028 NFL Draft Round 1: Own, Patriots (Brown trade) Round 2: Own, Ravens (Jurgens trade) Round 3: Own Round 4: Own Round 5: Own Round 6: Own Round 7: Own 2029 NFL Draft Round 1: Own Round 2: Own, Jaguars (Davis trade) Round 3: Own Round 4: Own Round 5: Own Round 6: Own Round 7: Own FOX SPORTS NEWSLETTERYour teams. articles.title: Minnesota's Offense Comes Up Short: 3 Takeaways From The Bills' Monday Night Win
articles.summary: The Minnesota Vikings couldn't keep up with the Buffalo Bills on offense. Here are takeaways from Monday night's game.
articles.body: It certainly wasn’t pretty, but the Bills notched an important road win that kept them on top of the AFC standings, outlasting the Vikings in a 23-6 slugfest that won’t be featured in any end-of-season highlight reels for either team. Buffalo struggled to move the ball against the Vikings' elite defense before eventually breaking through. A dismal performance from Carson Wentz, who was filling in for an injured Kyler Murray, certainly helped the Bills' cause. The journeyman backup wasted several opportunities to stake Minnesota to a first-half lead and eventually left the game to a chorus of boos at home. From there, it was only a matter of time before Josh Allen put the game away. Here are my takeaways: 1.The Vikings Don't Have A Solution To Their Embarrassing QB Play On Their Roster Barring a trade at the deadline, quarterback Kyler Murray’s job is safe. But the Vikings should really consider making a trade for a quarterback on Tuesday if it wants to salvage its season – or just give its fanbase an offense worth cheering for. It’s no exaggeration to call Wentz’s performance one of the worst we’ve seen from a quarterback in recent history. The Vikings defense tried its best to keep Minnesota in the game with timely stops, only to watch Wentz give the ball right back to Buffalo. Wentz's turnovers got progressively worse as the night went on. He was charged with a fumble after sailing a perimeter screen pass to Justin Jefferson, which was ruled a lateral on review. He sabotaged a promising second-half drive with an underthrown pass up the seam that linebacker Dorian Williams picked off. And then he followed that up with another pick after throwing the ball directly to linebacker Terrell Bernard. Outside those plays, Wentz was shockingly inaccurate. He missed several layup throws in the first quarter and never really recovered from there, finishing 8-for-25 for 81 yards and two interceptions before he was benched for third-stringer Max Brosmer in garbage time. Murray’s performance this season looks solid compared to what we saw on Monday night, but with veteran options like Kirk Cousins and Geno Smith potentially available on the trade market, the Vikings front office has to seriously consider a trade. It would be an insult to defensive coordinator Brian Flores’ unit not to. Minnesota has a Super Bowl-caliber defense that proved itself once again against the league’s highest-scoring offense. For a second consecutive week, though, the defense buckled under the pressure the failing offense is putting it under. Allen eventually found a groove in the second half and put up just enough points to put the game out of reach. 2.Josh Allen Tames The NFL's Best Defense Like most teams, the Bills found no success on the ground against a stout Vikings front. Typically, fielding a one-dimensional game against Minnesota is a recipe for disaster, but not when you have Josh Allen. While Allen didn’t put up a gaudy stat line – throwing for 234 yards and just one touchdown – he did carry the Bills offense with his playmaking. He threw the game’s first touchdown after leaving the pocket, buying extra time, and launching a deep ball over the Vikings secondary to reserve tight end Keleki Latu in the back of the end zone. In the first half, it felt like Allen creating out of structure was the only way Buffalo would move the ball, but cracks in Minnesota’s pass coverage eventually emerged the longer its defense remained on the field. Allen started hitting passes in rhythm, causing the Vikings to adjust and give up more space in the run game. Running back James Cook was bottled up for most of the night, averaging just 3.5 yards per carry, but was the engine on the 15-play touchdown drive that put the game away. Allen didn’t escape the game without a mistake. He was picked off in the first quarter after launching a deep ball on third-and-23. The ball hung up in the air long enough for Vikings cornerback Bryon Murphy to vacate his coverage on the opposite side of the field and run under the ball. It was more of a bad throw than a bad decision, but we can’t write this one as an "arm punt," as it cost the Bills a chance at a field goal. Still, not many quarterbacks have fared as well against this defense as Allen did on Monday night. 3.Buffalo's Defense Looked Better, But It Needs Improvements Buffalo has given up only 16 points in its last two games. It would be easier to celebrate that achievement if those games weren’t against the Ravens' backup quarterbacks and Wentz. The Bills defense is showing some signs of improvement. The pass rush generated pressure on 41.2% of Minnesota’s dropbacks, per Next Gen Stats. Pass coverage is still a concern, though. There were a decent number of open throws to be made; Wentz just wasn’t capable of making them. Whether or not Buffalo can sustain this against better competition, the secondary could use an addition at the deadline. The team has been linked with Cardinals safety Budda Baker, and with the Jaguars trading for Jessie Bates on Monday, the Bills could be the only contending team in the market for a safety. A trade for a cornerback would also help, and with several veteran options, including Riq Woolen (Eagles), Donte Jackson (Chargers) and Nahshon Wright (Jets) available, the price for an upgrade shouldn’t be too steep. 3 ½. What's Next? After escaping Minnesota and its terrifying defense with a win, Buffalo gets a relatively easy two-week stretch before a brutal five-week gauntlet against the Chiefs, Patriots, Packers, Bears, and Broncos. The Bills have the inside track to the AFC’s top seed, but they will need to be at the top of their game through the holiday season to maintain it. Things won’t get any easier for a Vikings team desperately searching for an answer to its quarterback problem. They’ll travel to Green Bay next week for an important divisional game against the Packers, then head to Mexico City to take on the 49ers. Win those games, and Minnesota can re-establish itself as an NFC contender. Lose them, and the Vikings could fall out of the playoff race. articles.title: FIA chief says Qatar and Abu Dhabi Grand Prix to go ahead despite tensions
articles.summary: This year’s Saudi Arabian Grand Prix was scrapped following the outbreak of the US and Israel’s war with Iran.
articles.body:
The final races of the Formula One (F1) season in Qatar and Abu Dhabi will go ahead as planned despite tensions in the Middle East, the president of motorsports’ governing body Mohammed Ben Sulayem has said.

The last two grands prix of the year are scheduled for November 29 in Qatar and December 6 in Abu Dhabi.

The Saudi Arabia Grand Prix earlier this year was scrapped following the outbreak of the United States and Israel’s war with Iran , while the Bahrain race was delayed and moved to Malaysia.

“We are ready for Qatar and Abu Dhabi,” said Ben Sulayem, president of the Federation Internationale de l’Automobile (FIA), on social media on Tuesday.

“We are fully prepared and committed to delivering two outstanding grands prix weekends and a spectacular conclusion to the Formula One World Championship.

“We look forward to welcoming drivers, teams and fans to two iconic circuits for an unforgettable finish to the season. See you on the grid.”

Ben Sulayem’s comments echo those made by F1 boss Stefano Domenicali last month.

F1 drivers have expressed mixed feelings about racing in the Middle East, with four-time world champion Max Verstappen among those to air his reservations.

Italian youngster Kimi Antonelli has already wrapped up the drivers’ world championship title, while his Mercedes team secured the constructors’ crown last weekend in Sao Paulo.

Several events in Saudi Arabia, which borders Qatar and the United Arab Emirates, have been cancelled or postponed in recent weeks following attacks on the country by Yemen’s Houthis .

articles.title: Iraq bars Iranian football team’s plane from landing in Basra: Report
articles.summary: Decision by the Iraqi Civil Aviation Authority reportedly related to ⁠US sanctions imposed on Iranian airlines.
articles.body:
Iraq barred a plane carrying Iran’s national football ⁠team from ⁠landing at Basra airport on Tuesday, a decision by the Iraqi Civil Aviation Authority linked to ⁠ sanctions by the United States imposed on Iranian airlines, two Basra airport officials told the Reuters news agency.

The plane returned to Iran and landed ⁠at Abadan airport, and the team will now travel by road to Basra, an Iranian consulate official in Basra said.

The Iranian team was travelling to Iraq to participate in a ‌four-nation tournament in Basra also involving Iraq, Lebanon and Palestine.

An Iraqi civil aviation official said Iraq made the decision because it could not risk violating US sanctions on Iranian airlines.

The incident highlights the increasing impact of US sanctions on Iranian aviation operations in Iraq. ⁠

Washington announced sanctions on any global companies doing business with Iranian airlines after September 23, aiming to ground Iran’s entire civil fleet worldwide.

In September, Iraq ordered the suspension of Iranian flights to Baghdad airport after the US threatened secondary sanctions against airports and service providers that handle Iranian carriers.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned that airports servicing Iranian airlines could face sanctions, including exclusion from the US ‌dollar system.

This warning was part of a broader effort to tighten restrictions on Iran’s transport sector and on ‌foreign ‌entities providing services to sanctioned Iranian airlines.

Intensified sanctions are part of a US bid to squeeze Iran economically as President Donald Trump struggles to end the war that the US and Israel launched on the country in February.

articles.title: El Ice Team español se lanza a por todas
articles.standfirst: Reúne a siete deportistas y aspira a competir en tres disciplinas olímpicas en los Juegos de 2030
articles.summary: Reúne a ocho deportistas y aspira a competir en tres disciplinas olímpicas en los Juegos de 2030
articles.body: Hace 21 años, Ander Mirambell recorría los circuitos de skeleton en solitario, con su Ford Fiesta como compañero de viaje. Hoy, el escenario es muy diferente en el hielo español. Siete deportistas integran el Ice Team español, un proyecto que aspira a estar presente en tres disciplinas olímpicas en 2030: monobobsleigh, bobsleigh a dos y skeleton. Mirambell, actual director deportivo de la Federación Española de Deportes de Hielo, guía el proyecto con la vista puesta en los próximos Juegos. Antes de dejar su cargo como vicepresidente de la Federación Internacional, contribuyó a definir el nuevo sistema de clasificación olímpica, que tendrá en cuenta los mejores resultados de los dos años previos en vez de, como hasta ahora, los de la última temporada. La regularidad será determinante. "Este año es importante para probarlo todo, detectar los fallos y corregirlos de cara al siguiente. Así llegaremos con los deberes hechos a las dos temporadas que contarán para la clasificación olímpica. Quien empiece el próximo curso ya irá tarde", explica Mirambell desde Lillehammer, donde el equipo completó los primeros entrenamientos. El proceso de selección para el skeleton ha dejado dos nuevas incorporaciones: Jorge Bastos (Cádiz, 2000) y Javier Tovar (Valencia, 2002). Ambos proceden del atletismo y se suman a un grupo en el que ya estaban Adrián Rodríguez, que debutó en la Copa del Mundo en 2023, y Emily María Macdonald, que el pasado año acumuló sus primeras bajadas en la Copa de América. Bastos acredita 10.87 en los 100 metros. "Me presenté al proceso de selección porque el deporte me llamaba la atención y vi que mi perfil era compatible con los requisitos que pedían y me animé a probarlo", apunta el gaditano. Ha salido encantado de esta primera toma de contacto en Lillehammer. "Las primeras bajadas fueron impactantes. Te lo imaginas de una manera, pero la realidad es diferente. Al ir sumando bajadas era más consciente de lo que hacía y lo disfrutaba, siempre con la tensión que te hace estar alerta en la salida, pero al final de cada bajada esa sensación de adrenalina y velocidad es un gustazo", explica Bastos Tovar, con 10.90 en sus piernas, descubrió la disciplina viendo los Juegos de Invierno por televisión. "Vi que mucha gente hacía atletismo antes de hacer skeleton y me pareció atractiva la parte de correr y, sobre todo, del pilotaje". Antes de probarlo sobre el hielo, incluso había experimentado con él a través de un videojuego. Acumula más de diez bajadas y ha descubierto las exigencias de una disciplina en la que cada detalle cuenta."Lo que más me ha sorprendido ha sido la velocidad, las fuerzas G y cómo entrar en una curva unas décimas de segundo más tarde te puede cambiar toda la trayectoria. Todo es milimétrico", explica. Tovar compaginará el skeleton con el atletismo al aire libre. "Trataré de ir al Campeonato de España absoluto en 200 metros y en 4x100 con mi club", apunta. Bastos tiene claro cuál es su objetivo esta temporada: "Enamorarme del deporte y de momento vamos bien. Esta primera experiencia en Lillehammer me ha encantado el ambiente, la sensación de velocidad, el equipo... Y luego quiero desarrollarme como piloto: sumar bajadas e ir corrigiendo errores". "Bastos y Tovar tienen buena punta de velocidad, pero les falta peso en el trineo", analiza Mirambell. Ambos competirán en la Copa de Europa, al igual que Macdonald, cuya trayectoria guarda similitudes con la de Leanna García. Nacida en Gran Bretaña y con antepasados españoles, Emily María Macdonald, de 26 años y saltadora de pértiga, contactó con Mirambell a través de Instagram para trasladarle su deseo de competir por España. Superó las pruebas físicas de la selección británica, pero fue descartada por su estatura. "Cometieron un error porque tiene un potencial enorme. Ahora debe sumar bajadas en el trineo para seguir avanzando", apunta Mirambell. Macdonald encontró una oportunidad para desarrollar su carrera en el hielo con el equipo español. Compite con licencia por el País Vasco, ya que su familia tiene raíces en Bilbao. "Es fantástico formar parte del equipo español y me siento increíblemente afortunada y orgullosa de poder representar a España. Tengo muchas ganas de ver lo que podemos conseguir juntos esta temporada. Estoy muy contenta con cómo ha ido todo en Lillehammer. Hemos trabajado muchísimo. Estoy especialmente emocionada de competir en la Copa de Europa", comenta Emily María Macdonald. La continuidad en el equipo lleva el nombre de Adrián Rodríguez (Castro Urdiales, 1996), representante español en la Copa del Mundo. Esta temporada estrenará un trineo de gama alta, al que deberá adaptarse, y contará con la entrenadora surcoreana Rayoung Mun, que aportará conocimientos y una perspectiva diferentes a los de Mirambell. “El objetivo es llegar bien al Mundial de Lillehammer de 2027. Entre la Copa del Mundo y la Copa de Europa podrá probar el trineo y adaptarse a él”, explica el director deportivo, que cerró su carrera en los circuitos con más de 180 competiciones, 92 en la Copa del Mundo. La otra gran apuesta está en el bobsleigh. Leanna García seguirá como piloto y en Lillehammer se estrenaron tres nuevas frenadoras: Danae Trinidad, Patricia Urquía y Lola Sánchez. La ampliación responde también a los cambios que estudia la Federación Internacional. Contempla eliminar las plazas olímpicas exclusivas para el monobobsleigh. Habría que conseguir previamente un billete en bobsleigh a dos o a cuatro. Leanna García compaginará las dos disciplinas. La canadiense, con raíces españolas, obtuvo el pasaporte nacional en el verano de 2024. En noviembre de ese año debutó con un quinto puesto en la Copa América de Whistler (Canadá). Unos meses después, en marzo, se convirtió en la primera mujer española de la historia en disputar un Mundial de monobobsleigh. Las frenadoras provienen de disciplinas diferentes. Trinidad, de 30 años, procede del CrossFit; Urquía, de 27 años, llega del atletismo, donde se especializó en los 200 metros. Dos graves lesiones de rodilla marcaron su trayectoria. Tras dejar el CAR de Sant Cugat, regresó a La Rioja y pidió a Mirambell la oportunidad de realizar las pruebas de selección. Las superó y se ganó un sitio en el equipo. Lola Sánchez, de 29 años, procede del lanzamiento de disco. También superó las pruebas y destacó especialmente en la valoración psicológica. Las bajadas en el circuito noruego sirvieron para ver a las tres en acción, ya que la idea era elegir una frenadora titular y otra reserva. Lola Sánchez, finalmente, quedó fuera del proyecto. Alguna de las dos elegidas puede probar ya este año como piloto. El proyecto cuenta con el respaldo de 'Titans', una iniciativa coordinada por Jo Manning, entrenadora con seis participaciones olímpicas. Llevó a Jamaica a los Juegos de 2018, a Brasil a los de 2026 y a Países Bajos hasta el cuarto puesto en Sochi 2014. “Me gusta el desafío de ayudar a los equipos a hacer historia. El objetivo de España encaja muy bien con esa filosofía”, explica. La colaboración permite que los equipos femeninos de Brasil, España y Letonia compartan estructura y recursos, desde entrenadores hasta fisioterapeutas y mecánicos, con el objetivo de reducir costes. Una fórmula que facilita el acceso a servicios que resultarían difíciles de asumir de manera individual. “Sin algo así no podríamos crear una curva de aprendizaje tan alta”, apunta Mirambell. Manning, responsable del programa que llevó al equipo femenino británico al oro mundial en 2009, también destaca la evolución de las nuevas integrantes españolas. “Me impresiona mucho lo que he visto de las chicas y cómo se han adaptado estos primeros días”. La Federación Española de Deportes de Hielo ha reforzado además el acompañamiento psicológico. Carlos de la Torre se trasladó con la expedición a Lillehammer para mejorar la gestión mental y del grupo. “Los nuevos han llegado con más confianza que en años anteriores. Es un punto diferencial”, destaca Mirambell. La apuesta actual contrasta con los comienzos del propio Mirambell, hace 21 años con unos ralladores de queso en las zapatillas. “Hace 21 años estaba yo solo y ahora ves este equipazo. Más de lo que hacemos es imposible”, destaca Ander. Pese a recibir ofertas de otros países con opciones claras de medalla, decidió renovar con España. Su objetivo va más allá de los resultados inmediatos. "Me hace más feliz dejar un legado y trabajar para que los deportes de hielo sigan creciendo aquí. Sé que ganar una medalla me subiría el ego, pero cuando me retire prefiero recordar que puse una semilla para el desarrollo del bobsleigh y el skeleton en España. Eso no tiene precio", sentencia Mirambell, cuatro veces olímpico, pionero y ahora impulsor de este nuevo 'milagro' del hielo español.

articles.title: Hulk Hogan’s memorial foundation aims to support children, students and families through scholarships, sports programmes and medical assistance after the wrestling icon’s death
articles.summary: Hulk Hogan spent much of his public life under the lights of wrestling arenas, where his name became familiar to audiences around the world.
articles.body: Hulk Hogan spent much of his public life under the lights of wrestling arenas, where his name became familiar to audiences around the world. Away from the ring, however, he also had connections with charitable causes involving children, young people, veterans and families facing difficult circumstances. Following his death, that part of his life has become the focus of a new fundraising effort. The Hulk Hogan Charitable Foundation Fund, established in his memory, is intended to support organisations and individuals working across education, sport, healthcare and community development.How Hulk Hogan’s foundation continues his charitable legacyThe Hulk Hogan Charitable Foundation Fund was created to carry forward the wrestler’s involvement with charitable work. It operates through the Pinellas Community Foundation, a Florida-based philanthropic organisation that provides a route for donations to reach eligible causes.The fund’s stated purpose extends beyond a single charity or community project. Its remit includes supporting vulnerable individuals and families, helping young people access opportunities and backing registered non-profit organisations whose work relates to athletics, medical needs, education and community development.The initiative also gives donors a way to contribute to causes associated with Hogan’s public and personal life. Rather than being limited to one specific programme, the fund has been set up to support a range of activities that fit within its charitable objectives.Scholarships, sports and support for familiesYoung people and families are among the groups identified in the fund’s plans. Its stated areas of support include scholarships, sports programmes and wellness initiatives, with direct assistance intended for people who may otherwise struggle to access those opportunities.Sports form a clear part of the fund’s remit, reflecting Hogan’s long association with professional wrestling and athletics. Support for local sports organisations can help provide young people with access to organised activities, coaching and facilities. Scholarship assistance can also help students pursue further education or training.The fund is not restricted to youth sports, though. Its objectives include medical and educational support, alongside wider community development work. This gives it scope to assist non-profit organisations working with people at different stages of life and facing different challenges.Hulk Hogan’s charitable work supported sick children, veterans and young peopleHogan’s charitable activities included appearances connected with children facing serious illnesses. He took part in Make-A-Wish visits and supported children’s hospitals, bringing attention to the experiences of young patients and their families.His involvement also extended to veterans and young people considered at risk. Local sports teams and community causes were among the areas associated with his giving. These activities took place alongside a career that made him one of professional wrestling’s most recognisable figures.How the fund is intended to workThe Hulk Hogan Charitable Foundation Fund is designed to support eligible 501(c)(3) non-profit organisations, a category of charitable organisations recognised under United States tax law. The causes they serve must align with the fund’s stated areas, including athletics, healthcare, education and community development.Its objectives also allow for assistance to individuals and families. This includes support for young people through scholarships and sports activities, as well as wellness-related initiatives. The precise form of assistance can therefore depend on the needs of the recipients and the organisations involved.The Pinellas Community Foundation provides the donation channel. Its fund page continues to invite contributions, although the publicly available description does not provide a complete breakdown of money raised, grants awarded or the number of people helped since the fund was established. articles.title: College Basketball Catchup: Indiana-Syracuse, A 20-Rebound Game, Hurley Thoughts
articles.summary: A Syracuse freshman showed no fear in the paint, a freshman scoring record for Mizzou, a transfer showed off and more from Monday's college basketball action.
articles.body: Syracuse and Indiana fought to the end. A 20-rebound, 20-point double-double. A freshman scoring record, and a career-high. It wasn't a quiet November Monday in college basketball by any means. Here's what you need to know from yesterday's slate of college basketball. You Have To See This You know what makes a serious difference in the performance of a guard? A lack of fear. Sure, you might miss a layup. You might get rejected at the basket. You also might get fouled and go to the line, or maybe, just maybe, break through the defense and score despite the odds. Ryan Moesch is a guard for Syracuse, and the Orange freshman stands just six feet tall, per Syracuse’s own numbers. And on Monday night against Indiana, Moesch went right at 7-foot-2 Hoosier center Samet Yigitoglu in the paint. And Moesch came out ahead in that encounter. That kind of aggressiveness, that lack of hesitation, is vital for a guard. There is always going to be someone taller lurking in the paint. Someone who could swat both you and the ball away with a thought. Learning to work around their existence, though? That’s a huge part of the job, and Moesch is showing a willingness to attack early in his collegiate career. The game didn’t go Syracuse’s way in the end, with Indiana winning 83-80. Still, a great effort from Moesch and the Orange against a Big Ten opponent in non-conference play, despite the first loss of Gerry McNamara’s run as Orange coach. Top Performance: Tatum West Tatum West played just 22 minutes for Northern Colorado on Monday, but she made them count. While taking on NAIA’s Northern New Mexico, the senior forward put on a show: she shot 9-for-12 and hit six of nine free throws, blocked two shots, grabbed a steal and pulled down 20 rebounds to go with her 24 points. That’s a double-double and then some. Of those rebounds, 12 of them were actually offensive boards: given her shooting percentage, it wasn’t her misses she was grabbing, either. She was doing work under the basket for everyone else. West also had two assists — you can see one of those dimes, a real quick-thinking pass back outside, below. Sure, an NAIA opponent is the kind a Division I school like Northern Colorado is going to plow through, but it’s not like West has never performed before. As a junior playing Big Sky ball for Northern Colorado last season, she averaged 11.2 points per game and pulled down 9.1 rebounds while grabbing two steals and nearly 1.5 assists per game. She also shot just under 59% — West is an efficient player who has gotten better every year, and could be taking one more leap as a senior. Men's Scoring Leader: Jason Crowe Jr. Jason Crowe Jr. set the freshman rookie scoring record for Missouri on Monday night, while facing SIU Edwardsville. The 6-foot-4 guard shot 11-for-16 overall and 4-for-8 from beyond the arc, to go along with eight makes in nine trips to the line to finish with 34 points. He also grabbed a pair of boards and logged four assists. Through three games, Crowe is averaging 21.7 points with 4.3 assists. It should be noted, though, especially with the small sample, that his worst performance so far came against the toughest opponent Missouri has had: Saint Louis. Still, seven dimes was encouraging, and maybe the shots will fall next time. Women's Scoring Leader: Petra Božan Petra Božan, a junior transfer from Nebraska to Penn State, did basically one thing on Monday: score. The 6-foot-4 forward has never been much of a rebounder, and on Monday she had just one board to keep that going. What she did have was her shot from three, though: Božan launched six triples and sank five of them, and made every shot from inside the arc to finish with 27 points on 10-for-11 shooting. While this was a career high for Božan — her previous best was 17 in a game last December, coincidentally against Penn State — it wasn’t enough to get the Nittany Lions past Dayton. The The Flyers won, 77-71, and Penn State is now 0-3 on the year. One Name To Know: Matas Vokietaitis Center Matas Vokietaitis is in his second season with Texas. The seven-foot, 255 pounder has been capable of being a problem underneath for opponents in the past: while he’s not the rebounder you think he would be given his size, he does use it to get himself into position to score against opponents who can’t stop him. He led the SEC in field goal percentage in the 2025-2026 season, shooting just a hair under 62% for the year. Obviously, SEC play hasn’t begun yet, but Vokietaitis has started out hot in 2026-2027. Monday against Grambling was his best outing so far, with nine rebounds, a block, a steal and 26 points on 8-for-12 shooting. The thing to watch the most with him, though, is how often he’s called for fouls. If he can be smarter about not picking up fouls, that’s huge: he led the SEC with 123 of them last season, but has forced just one whistle in two of his three games so far. He’s at 38.2 points per 40 minutes as well as 13.1 rebounds, and while he’s played 22.3 minutes per game in actuality, that’s the kind of leap in performance that can come when you don’t have to worry as much about an extra bump putting you in foul trouble. So, if the fouls are reduced, he can be the monster he’s capable of in the paint — which would be bad news for opposing offenses and defenses. Before You Go: Dan Hurley's Thoughts UConn played Wagner on Monday, which isn’t notable on its own: Wagner is a very small private college with around 2,000 total students, known more for its academics than its athletics, and UConn was just in the national championship game once again in the spring. However, the Seahawks been a jumping off point for a number of successful college coaches elsewhere, including but not limited to the Huskies’ current head coach, Dan Hurley, who coached the Seahawks from 2010 to 2012 before making the jump to Rhode Island, his last gig before coming to Connecticut. Hurley spoke on what memories facing off against his former team brought back to the surface for him following Monday’s 83-41 victory by No. 4 UConn, and how they shaped the coach he is now. "I felt like I was coaching the Celtics. I felt like the fate of the free world depended on whether we won or lost games or not." Dan Hurley, living or dying on every play and game? Hard to believe he’d ever be like that. articles.title: Fantasy Football Panic Meter: Matthew Stafford heads to Coping Corner after Puka Nacua injury
articles.summary: Ray Garvin highlights the concern level for 6 players for fantasy football going into Week 10.
articles.body:
At this point in the season, we have to adjust our expectations. Some of these players still belong in your fantasy football lineup, but that doesn't mean you should feel good about them. The categories remain No Panic, Some Panic, Total Panic and Coping Corner. Nobody here gets No Panic from me.

Jonathan Taylor, RB, Colts: Total Panic if he stays

If Jonathan Taylor stays in Indianapolis, I have total panic. Total panic.

Over the last two games, Taylor has combined for 21 carries, 69 rushing yards and no touchdowns. With two lost fumbles, he's averaged 5.8 half-PPR points. His carries dropped from 21 and 18 in Weeks 6 and 7 to 8 and 13 in Weeks 8 and 9.

He was productive in those earlier games. This hasn't been a month of nothing. But the direction should concern everybody who has Taylor.

I'm watching this usage and wondering whether the Colts are holding him back for a trade. I don't know that. I do know I want him out of there.

I don't trust this offense with Daniel Jones. Indianapolis also traded Quenton Nelson, its All-Pro guard and, in everyone's opinion, its best offensive lineman.

Taylor is a running back who can catch passes. He is not a pass-catching weapon who plays running back. His nine catches over the last two games produced 42 yards. That hasn't come close to rescuing him from bad rushing days.

And I expect the Colts to spend plenty of time trailing. That's a problem when the passing game isn't giving their best offensive player much help.

I'd love a move that gives Taylor a chance to thrive. If he's banished to this offense, we should be very, very concerned.

Every week, there's another reason to believe the Chase Brown game is coming. The receiving work. The offense. The matchup. Then we're disappointed again.

Brown hasn't scored a rushing touchdown since Week 1. That's seven games and 87 carries. He hasn't scored a receiving touchdown or reached 100 rushing yards in a game this season either. He's averaged 8.6 half-PPR points over his last four appearances. Cincinnati scored at least 31 points in all four. This offense is producing. Brown just isn't getting enough of the fantasy payoff.

Joe Burrow is playing at an MVP level with 23 passing touchdowns. The Bengals have five rushing touchdowns as a team. This offense runs through Burrow. Brown can help with dump-offs when Cincinnati is chasing points, but those receiving spikes are hard to predict. He caught eight passes in Week 8 and three the following week.

I've got Some Panic because I know what I'm getting: a volatile mid-to-low-end RB2 with sporadic receiving upside. I'm done treating every week like the breakout is right around the corner.

I talked about this on the Yahoo Data Dump show. I've been concerned about Derrick Henry.

The crown has fallen. He is no longer the king.

Henry is 32, and Father Time always wins. Give him a runway and he can still get north and south quickly. But I'm not seeing him make defenders miss the way this offense needs him to, and I think this offensive line has been dreadful. The season totals look fine until you're actually living with these afternoons.

Seven of his eight rushing touchdowns came in the first four weeks. Over his last four games, Henry has 62 carries for 213 yards and one rushing touchdown. That's 3.4 yards per carry. He's added four catches for 13 yards.

Baltimore scored 10, 13, 10 and 10 points in those games. Its last three losses were all by at least 20 points. The defense isn't keeping games close, and the offense isn't creating enough scoring opportunities.

Could Jacoby Brissett help? Sure. Jesse Minter says Brissett is going to start in Week 10. But I need to see it. Brissett doesn't immediately fix the blocking, the defense or my concerns about Henry himself. Total Panic. You're playing him as a mid-to-low-end RB2 right now.

Jayden Daniels, QB, Commanders: Some Panic

The only reason Jayden Daniels isn't in Total Panic is that my expectations have been adjusted. I hope yours have, too. He returned from the elbow injury in Week 5 and ran for 103 yards and two touchdowns. The rushing alone gave you 22.3 fantasy points.

Since then, he has 10 carries for 49 yards and no rushing touchdowns across three games. That's about 1.6 fantasy points per game from rushing.

The passing hasn't completely fallen apart. Daniels threw for 300 yards and two touchdowns in Week 6. But his last two fantasy scores were 14.98 and 14.56. Without the rushing advantage, there's much less room for an ordinary passing performance.

Terry McLaurin is out for the season, and Washington doesn't have many pass-catching options to replace him. The margin for success is smaller.

I've got Some Panic because I'm no longer expecting Daniels to automatically give me the advantage I drafted him for. If there's a better weekly streaming option, I'm considering it. He's no longer a must-play quarterback for me.

Matthew Stafford, QB, Rams: Coping Corner

I have total, total panic about this situation. Matthew Stafford belongs in Coping Corner. He wasn't giving us enough with Puka Nacua. Now, Puka is likely headed to injured reserve with MCL and PCL sprains along with turf toe. Stafford has averaged 200.5 passing yards and 13.47 fantasy points over his last four games. He hasn't reached 250 passing yards in any of them. His last two fantasy scores were 8.28 and 11.22.

We were already talking ourselves into starting him. Now, we're taking away his best receiving option. Head coach Sean McVay expects Davante Adams back toward the shorter end of his 6-10 week window. But what does "sooner" mean for your lineup right now?

Stafford is 38, and to me, he's showing his age. His right elbow was on the Week 9 injury report, although he practiced fully. I can't tell you the elbow explains everything, but this situation gives me little confidence.

With Puka, Stafford was streamable. Without Puka and Davante, he's a quarterback I have zero interest in starting.

Drake London is in Total Panic, too. Michael Penix Jr. has not been good. This offense has not been good. London is still Atlanta's leading receiver, but that doesn't make me feel better about the situation.

Over his last four games, London has 17 catches for 204 yards and one touchdown, averaging 8.7 half-PPR points. Over the last two, he has six catches for 76 yards and no touchdowns.

Penix has combined for 287 passing yards, one touchdown and five interceptions across those two games. How much confidence are we supposed to have in London delivering WR1 production in that environment? London has 692 receiving yards this season, so there have been productive games. But he has one receiving touchdown, and this recent connection hasn't been good enough.

You drafted him in the first round to be your WR1. This isn't close to what you needed.

I have low faith in Penix right now, and that directly affects how I feel about London.

The talent hasn't changed. My confidence in this offense consistently getting that talent into your fantasy lineup has. I'm not comfortable pretending the situation is fine.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Start 'Em, Sit 'Em: RBs in timeshares you can trust in Week 10 lineups
articles.summary: Fantasy analyst Fred Zinkie takes a look at some unsettled backfields across the NFL to see who could be lineup option in Week 10.
articles.body:
Let's take a look at the backup RBs who have a Yahoo roster rate under 60% and could help fantasy teams to victory in Week 10. Players are ranked in order of their Week 10 appeal, and their current roster rates are listed in parentheses.

Each week, Kiner becomes more appealing. Things continued to trend in his direction in Week 9, starting with information leading up to the game that TreVeyon Henderson is dealing with neurological symptoms. The absence of Henderson pushed Kiner up to the RB2 position, and he averaged 6.9 yards on eight carries in a lopsided loss to the Packers.

The second-year pro has averaged over 5.0 yards per carry in four of the Patriots past five games, while starter Rhamondre Stevenson is averaging just 3.9 yards per carry this season. Comparing the two players for Week 10 is a moot point, since Stevenson is expected to miss time with a knee injury . Kiner is a RB2 option for a potential shootout against the Lions, and he could carve out a permanent role by the time Stevenson returns.

With Kendre Miller off the roster and Alvin Kamara past the point in his career where he can handle a heavily workload, Estime was the lead runner in a dramatic Week 9 win over the Browns. The 23-year-old collected 72 yards and a touchdown on 15 carries, while ceding most of the passing game work to Kamara.

The Saints have been quiet on the progress of Travis Etienne Jr., who has been on injured reserve since suffering a hamstring strain in Week 3. Etienne's 21-day practice window has yet to be opened, which means that Estime could handle a heavy workload once again in Week 10, when the Saints host a Panthers team that has allowed the second-most fantasy points per game to opposing RBs. Estime is a borderline RB2 for that game.

At this point, it's undeniable that Kaelon Black has a significant role in the 49ers offense. The rookie gained 70 yards on 11 carries in a lopsided Week 9 win over the Raiders, while starter Christian McCaffrey continued to receive a heavy workload that was divided between the rushing and passing game.

Head coach Kyle Shanahan has compensated for multiple WR injuries by maximizing the use of his RBs, and Black has responded by averaging 4.5 yards per carry. Black's lack of involvement in the passing game limits his upside, but he still carries some flex appeal into a Week 10 matchup against a porous Cowboys defense that has allowed the fifth-most fantasy points per game to opposing RBs.

This is a big day for McGowan, who could be the Colts starting RB by 4 p.m. ET. And even if Jonathan Taylor remains with the Colts, there seems to be a role for McGowan, who scored and gained 45 yards on six carries in Week 9. McGowan is averaging 4.8 yards per carry in his rookie season and has averaged six carries in his past six games. Meanwhile, Taylor's snap share has consistently dipped throughout the campaign, going from 85% or higher in the initial three games to below 70% in each of the past two contests.

The Colts could continue to move in a run-heavy direction thanks to the disappointing results from Daniel Jones. A Week 10 home game against the low-scoring Dolphins would certainly be a good opportunity to play it safe with a heavy dose of Taylor and McGowan. And if Taylor is traded on Tuesday, McGowan will become an RB2 option for that game.

Tyler Allgeier came crashing back to earth after his memorable Week 8 performance, as the Seahawks defense held him to 46 total yards on 17 carries and two catches. The Cardinals coaching staff never really expected Allgeier to be the lead back in the first place, as they have often commented that he is best suited for a complementary role that includes significant usage in the passing game. With Jeremiyah Love on IR, Knight is well-positioned to lead the Cardinals in Week 10 carries, provided that he is ready to return from a concussion. Still, his upside is limited, given that the Cardinals have an unsettled QB situation and could be playing from behind against the Rams.

Josh Jacobs will almost certainly miss Week 10 and may land on IR while he recovers from surgery on a fractured finger that he suffered in a Week 9 win over the Patriots. With the Packers leading and Jacobs unavailable, they turned to Johnson to put the game away on the ground. Johnson responded by gaining 68 yards on 14 carries and scoring a touchdown in the team's surprising 45-point outburst. As per usual, he was not involved in the passing game, as those responsibilities were handled by Pierre Strong Jr.

With four teams on a bye and others dealing with injuries, Johnson is a strong flex option if MarShawn Lloyd misses a second straight game. The situation becomes more jumbled if Lloyd plays this week, as both he and Johnson would be weak flex options. The value of any Packers RB for Week 10 is also capped by a tough matchup against a Vikings defense that has allowed the eighth-fewest fantasy points per game to opposing running backs.

A change at QB didn't impact Sampson's role, as the change-of-pace back gained 48 total yards on eight carries and three catches in a Week 9 loss to the Saints. Sampson has 15 carries and 12 catches in three games since returning from IR, as he is clearly the RB who dominates passing game work over Quinshon Judkins. The Browns are underdogs in Week 10 against the Texans, and Sampson could score 5-10 points in PPR formats if they spend most of the game playing from behind.

Although Bhayshul Tuten has taken over as Jacksonville's lead back, he and Rodriguez have had similar success on the ground. After all, both players have scored four rushing touchdowns, while Tuten is averaging 4.3 yards per carry, in comparison to 4.1 yards for Rodriguez. If the recent usage continues in Week 10, Rodriguez will have roughly half as many carries as Tuten and will have little usage in the passing game. But with the Jaguars heading into a potentially lopsided matchup with the Titans, there could ample opportunity for both rushers.

Mitchell continued to fill the change-of-pace role in Week 9. The speedster ranked third among Los Angeles RBs in snap share, but he was more involved in the passing game than Omarion Hampton or Kimani Vidal.

The 0-8 Chargers are a mess offensively, and they are unlikely to turn things around in Baltimore on Monday Night Football. Still, those in PPR formats can expect 5-8 points from Mitchell, which may be the best available option for some managers in deep leagues.

Although Johnson is showing strong skills as a rookie, he is locked into a low-volume backup role behind superstar Kenneth Walker III. Still, the rookie managed to score a touchdown and gain 34 yards on six carries in a lopsided Week 9 win over the Jets. He could have a role in Week 10, when the Chiefs face a mediocre Falcons defense that has allowed the seventh-most fantasy points per game to opposing RBs.

The players listed below are unlikely to provide significant assistance in Week 10 but are an injury away from having significant value.

articles.title: WWE Rumors on Randy Orton's Future, Tiffany Stratton Backlash and Rhea Ripley's Return
articles.summary: Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.
articles.body:
Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.

Survivor Series Match Card Predictions 🔮

Randy Orton is reportedly expected to take some time away from WWE following his loss to Cody Rhodes at Crown Jewel on Saturday.

According to WrestleVotes on Fightful Select (h/t Geno Mrosko of Cageside Seats), Orton is not scheduled for the Survivor Series or Wrestlepalooza premium live events, and he is not expected back on WWE programming until after the holidays.

At Crown Jewel, Orton clashed with Rhodes in a highly physical and entertaining Last Man Standing match.

The Viper expressed doubt leading up to the match that Cody would be willing to do what he had to do in order to win the bout.

Rhodes proved him wrong, though, by punting Orton in the head, which kept him down long enough for the 10 count.

Orton's punt has been used to write wrestlers off television many times over the years, so it is fitting that The Apex Predator appears to be on the other end of it this time around.

Since the focus for Survivor Series is on the WarGames matches, which Orton was not going to be involved with, it makes sense to take him out of the equation and give him some time off.

WWE would undoubtedly love to have Orton fresh and healthy for WrestleMania season, so bringing him back for the Royal Rumble and the road to WrestleMania is likely the best course of action to ensure that is the case.

WWE's Reported Reaction to Criticism of Stratton

WWE reportedly isn't concerned with the negative response from some fans regarding Tiffany Stratton becoming the new WWE women's champion.

Stratton surprised many by turning on Chelsea Green at Crown Jewel, as she cashed in her Money in the Bank contract on Green rather than Liv Morgan en route to winning the WWE women's title.

Per Felix Upton of Ringside News, the YouTube video of Stratton cashing in had significantly more dislikes than likes as of Monday.

According to WrestleVotes on Fightful Select (h/t Upton ), WWE is perfectly fine with that, though, since the company feels a dislike is "just as good" as a like, "as long as there's an interaction."

Given that Tiffany's cash-in was essentially a heel turn, a strong argument can be made that the dislikes are a positive thing.

While the lines are often blurred in wrestling these days between babyfaces and heels, the traditional goal was always for the heel to be hated by fans.

It is clear that fans are not happy about the cash-in, and while there could be any number of reasons for that, WWE is getting the desired reaction.

Green has become a sentimental favorite among the WWE Universe, and the manner in which she lost the title should only serve to garner her more support, which plays right into the story WWE is attempting to tell.

Ripley's Reported Status for Wrestlepalooza

WWE is reportedly planning to have Rhea Ripley on hand for Wrestlepalooza next month in her home country of Australia.

According to WrestleVotes on Fightful Select (h/t H Jenkins of Ringside News), "all signs indicate" that Ripley will travel with WWE to Australia for Wrestlepalooza, although it isn't yet known if she will be cleared to wrestle by then.

Ripley has been out of action since June due to a knee injury that eventually required surgery .

Rhea was the WWE women's champion at the time of the injury, and while WWE initially sought to crown only an interim champ, her stay on the injured list ended up being a lengthy one, so the interim tag was removed after Green won the title in a ladder match at SummerSlam.

No official update has been provided regarding how longer Ripley may be on the shelf, but having her for Wrestlepalooza in any capacity would be a huge win for WWE.

She is one of the most popular members of the roster anywhere in the world, but that is especially true in her home country of Australia.

Just having her on hand to make an appearance would likely get people in the building, and WrestleVotes' report suggests WWE will indeed have her available.

articles.title: Bodhana Sivanandan: "Con cinco años, usaba las piezas como juguetes"
articles.standfirst: La inglesa de 11 años que bate todos los récords de precocidad femeninos, visita MARCA antes de participar en el Festival Internacional Salamanca Cuna del Ajedrez Moderno
articles.summary: Con 11 años, la inglesa que bate todos los récords de precocidad femeninos, visita MARCA antes de participar en el Festival Internacional Salamanca Cuna del Ajedrez Moderno
articles.body: Bodhana Sivanandan es locuaz para tener 11 años. Delante de un tablero es la reencarnación de Kali, pura energía; fuera de los escaques intenta ser una niña más de una barriada de Londres, donde nació y reside. Su precocidad en el ajedrez ha roto moldes históricos en un deporte que tiene más de 500 años. Visita la redacción de MARCA en una parada hacia el IX Festival Internacional Salamanca Cuna del Ajedrez Moderno, que tendrá el privilegio de tenerla en un plantel de lujo en un torneo que comienza el miércoles y concluye el sábado en la capital charra. Pregunta: Empezó a jugar al ajedrez a los 5 años, cuando el confinamiento por el COVID. ¿Qué fue lo primero que le atrajo del ajedrez? Respuesta: Lo primero fue el aspecto de las piezas, porque quería usarlas como juguetes fuera del ajedrez. Mi padre me dijo que, si lo hacía, la siguiente persona que usara ese tablero no podría jugar bien, así que me enseñó a jugar y me gustó. Empecé a jugar desde entonces. P. Va a la escuela con normalidad. ¿Cómo es su relación con los profesores y los compañeros de clase en Londres? R. Creo que tengo una buena relación, porque cuando estoy fuera del colegio por los torneos, no tengo problema en ponerme al día con los deberes. P. Supongo que sus compañeros le dicen cosas como "te vimos anoche en la BBC...." R. Sí, a veces lo dicen, pero normalmente en el colegio no hablamos mucho sobre ajedrez. P. Usted ha sido la gran maestra femenina más joven de la historia, más que Judith Polgar, y, fuera de géneros, uno de las maestras internacionales más jóvenes. ¿Qué significa para usted batir un récord así? R. Estoy contenta de haber batido un nuevo récord mundial, pero espero conseguir también el título de gran maestro (global) lo antes posible, seguir jugando y disfrutando del ajedrez. P. Representa a Inglaterra en el equipo nacional y fue la deportista más joven en hacerlo en cualquier deporte a la edad de 9 años. ¿Siente más presión cuando juega por equipos que de forma individual? R. No realmente, porque solo intento concentrarme en la partida. Si gano, es bueno para el equipo, por los puntos y cosas así. Incluso en equipo, solo intento concentrarme en el juego y no siento presión aparte de eso. P. Cuando era niña, el entonces primer ministro británico, Rishi Sunak, la invitó a jugar una partida en Downing Street. En abril, cuando se proclamó campeona británica, también la felicitó con un mensaje en Twitter que alcanzó 3,6 millones de visualizaciones. ¿Le dejó ganar o no? R. En realidad no jugué una partida en Downing Street. Fue una visita. Sobre el mensaje en Twitter, normalmente no miro las redes sociales, así que no lo vi. P. ¿Cómo lleva la fama? R. Solo intento jugar al ajedrez y, si llega la fama, hay que lidiar con ella. P. ¿Y sus padres? R. Probablemente tienen la misma actitud que yo. Solo me llevan a los torneos y, si sigo jugando y lo hago bien, obviamente la fama seguirá. P. ¿Su madre o su padre cocinan algo especial si gana un torneo? R. No, no realmente. P. ¿Cuánto tiempo dedica a entrenar cada día? R. Cuando voy al colegio a jornada completa, dos horas, contando el trabajo en casa y en el colegio. Los fines de semana puedo entrenar un poco más, porque no hay colegio. P. ¿Tiene algún tipo de descanso durante la temporada? R. Sí, a veces después de los torneos. P. ¿Cómo se siente cuando gana a un oponente mucho mayor que usted? R. Trato de no pensar en la edad durante la partida, así que normalmente me siento igual si gano a alguien de mi edad o a alguien mucho mayor. P. ¿Tiene alguna rutina antes de la partida? R. No, no tengo ninguna rutina. P. ¿Cómo pasa el tiempo fuera del ajedrez? R. Toco el violín y el piano, así que hago algo de música, y el colegio también ocupa mucho tiempo. P. ¿Encuentra alguna similitud entre la música y el ajedrez? R. Sí, hay algunas similitudes. El reconocimiento de patrones es necesario tanto en el ajedrez como en la música, así que sí, en algunos sentidos. P. La derrota forma parte del deporte, obviamente. El antiguo campeón mundial Vesselin Topalov, al que verá en Salamanca, dice que ser un ganador es más difícil que perder una partida de ajedrez. ¿Qué hace para superar la derrota? R. Trato de tomarlo como un aprendizaje, en lugar de como una pérdida dura, y espero mejorar en la próxima partida. P. En una entrevista con MARCA, Carlsen dijo que los seres humanos somos muy malos jugando al ajedrez, al contrario que el ordenador. ¿Usa el ordenador como parte de su entrenamiento? R. Lo utilizo de vez en cuando, pero no demasiado. P. ¿Cómo se describiría como jugadora, en cuanto a su estilo de juego, y con qué jugador se identifica? R. Mi jugador favorito es Capablanca, porque era un jugador estratégico en los finales. Todos dicen que juego bien los finales, pero me gusta pensar en mí como una jugadora universal, que también sabe atacar. P. ¿Ha leído algo sobre él fuera del ajedrez? R. No, no mucho. P. ¿También le gusta el fútbol? Este fin de semana juegan España e Inglaterra. ¿Va a ver el partido, o no es muy aficionada? R. No, no veré el partido, ni siquiera sabía que lo jugaban hasta que me lo ha dicho. Pero a veces sigo los resultados, después de los partidos clave. Normalmente no veo partidos. P. ¿Escucha también música moderna? R. No, solo toco violín y piano. Aparte de eso, a veces escucho música, pero no en conciertos ni en directo. P. ¿Cuándo dejó de jugar con juguetes o con muñecas? R. Después de empezar a jugar al ajedrez, empecé a hacerlo con mucha intensidad, así que dejé los juguetes. Aún hoy, a veces juego un poco, pero no mucho. P. El año pasado, Faustino Oro recibió el premio MARCA a la mejor irrupción por encima de gente tan famosa como el futbolista Doué. ¿Le gustaría ganarlo algún año? R. Espero que sí P. Es impresionante el respaldo que tiene a su edad R. Si y aprovecho esta visita para agradecer a mis patrocinadores, a la federación inglesa, a Everon New York, Tangram Therapeutics, John Robinson Youth Chess Trust, y a todos mis entrenadores, mentores y colaboradores.

articles.title: Everything Connor Hellebuyck Said About End of Jets Tenure, Devils Trade, More Ahead of Return
articles.summary: New Jersey Devils goaltender Connor Hellebuyck pointed to what he indicated was harassment of his family when explaining his request to leave the Winnipeg Jets after 11 years with the organization.
articles.body:
New Jersey Devils goaltender Connor Hellebuyck pointed to what he indicated was harassment of his family when explaining his request to leave the Winnipeg Jets after 11 years with the organization.

Hellebuyck discussed his trade request with reporters before a Tuesday night game during which he is slated to back up Jake Allen in his return to Winnipeg.

"I will say, with all the uncertainty I was experiencing, there was some moments and some things that happened to my family that, for me, crossed the line," Hellebuyck said. "And as a husband and a father, I felt made that decision very certain."

Hellebuyck had previously cited "some very challenging circumstances involving my family" in a social media statement explaining his trade request.

The Jets had Hellebuyck under contract through 2030-31 when he refused to report to training camp this fall. He was subsequently suspended before getting traded Oct. 24 to the Devils.

"When you make a decision like this, I feel like it's got to be all or nothing, and I don't want to separate my family at all," Hellebuyck said about sitting out training camp. "And if I did have to come back it was going to be one of those scenarios where it was just me, and I have two young kids."

Jets general manager Kevin Cheveldayoff said in September he hadn't been "fully aware of the extent" to which Hellebuyck's family had experienced harassment.

When asked about the Jets saying they hadn't been informed about the situation, Hellebuyck pointed to his family's desire for privacy.

"I don't want to try to ruin the relationship I have with the city, because I'm not going to project a few moments on the entire city... but there are a few moments that I don't want to see happen again," Hellebuyck said.

"And it is more than just online death threats... There is more that made me and my family uncomfortable on top of some uncertainty with my career."

The former three-time Vezina Trophy winner is coming off a down final season with the Jets, during which he posted a career-low .895 save percentage as the franchise went 35-35-12 and missed the playoffs.

Hellebuyck also won Olympic gold in February with a United States team featuring multiple players, including Brady Tkachuk and Dylan Larkin, who have since requested trades from their respective NHL teams.

"Is there some difficulties with being an American playing in Canada? Definitely," Hellebuyck said. "But there's also a lot of positives... I don't want to say that there is a border issue in this decision."

Hellebuyck bounced back since his trade with a strong start to his first season with the Devils, marking a 5-0 record to go alongside a .913 save percentage and 1.96 goals against average in his first five starts.

Despite that early success the Devils announced this weekend Hellebuyck, who has started four of the team's last five games, would serve as backup during Tuesday night's game against the Jets.

General manager Sunny Mehta said in a Sunday statement the Devils were making the decision to start Allen because Hellebuyck "playing in this game would potentially give us a reduction in our expected win probability."

"I went in there and I said my piece. I said I felt it was my duty to play this game. I want to play," Hellebuyck said about wanting to start Tuesday. "And I had a good conversation with the coach, and Sunny, and I left that conversation understanding where they're at and why they're making that decision. I respect it."

Hellebuyck continued, "I'm kind of looking forward to seeing what this crowd's reaction is... However they want to bring their energy to the game, I embrace it."

The Jets have made their unhappiness with Hellebuyck clear since his departure. Kyle Connor, when asked about the trade in October, said he was excited to meet players who "want to be a part of Winnipeg Jets hockey." Coach Scott Arniel said Monday he felt Hellebuyck "gave up on us."

Hellebuyck didn't confirm whether he would be on the bench or watching from the video room Tuesday.

Either way Hellebuyck might be expecting a welcome similar to that received by Tkachuk, who was met by boos and chants when returning to Ottawa last month following his trade to the Florida Panthers, when the puck drops for Tuesday night's matchup at Canada Life Centre.

articles.summary: Los números 1 han anunciado su ausencia en la prueba emiratí por recomendación médica
articles.body: El P1 de Dubai de Premier Padel que se disputa esta semana en Emiratos Árabes ha sufrido una dura baja de última hora: los números 1, Agustín Tapia y Arturo Coello. Los 'Golden Boys', que confirmaron de forma matemática su reinado por cuarto curso consecutivo en el Major de Kuwait de hace dos semanas, han anunciado de forma conjunta hoy que no estarán en el torneo emiratí debido a una recomendación médica. "Sentimos tener que comunicar que no podremos competir esta semana en UAE por indicaciones médicas de nuestro equipo. Tras valorarlo conjuntamente, hemos tomado esta decisión pensando en lo mejor para nosotros y para poder volver a competir en las mejores condiciones lo antes posible. Esperamos que nos volvamos a ver muy pronto. Muchas gracias por la comprensión y el cariño de estos días", dice el anunciado de ambos. Ambos vienen de realizar un gran esfuerzo en el Mundial que se acabó llevando España -con los dos jugadores disputando un partido de la gran final- y ahora afrontarán dos semanas de descanso antes del último Major del 2026 que se disputa la semana del 23 de noviembre. De esta forma, el torneo se queda sin los dos primeros cabezas de serie, ya que Galán y Chingotto tampoco se inscribieron debido a la lesión que sufre el madrileño.

articles.title: Justin Jefferson should be happiest man alive after Vikings’ Kirk Cousins trade
articles.summary: Justin Jefferson now has room to shine again after the Minnesota Vikings acquired Kirk Cousins before the trade deadline.
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings finally have an answer for Justin Jefferson, and it is a familiar face who could help bring the best out of their superstar receiver again. Minnesota has reunited with Kirk Cousins , acquiring the veteran quarterback from the Las Vegas Raiders before the NFL trade deadline. For Jefferson, it is an opportunity to reconnect with a veteran player who already knows how to get him the football and helped him produce some of the best numbers of his career.

Jefferson has not been quite the same dominant force this season, with Minnesota's quarterback situation contributing to an offense that has struggled to find consistency. While he remains one of the most talented players at his position, his production has taken a noticeable dip compared with what Vikings fans have come to expect.

But having a quarterback like Cousins who understands his routes, timing and tendencies could make a significant difference during the second half of the season.

Justin Jefferson's production has taken a significant dip

The numbers show why Cousins' return is beyond welcoming for Jefferson. According to SumerSports figures, Jefferson averaged 108.2 receiving yards and 0.5 touchdowns per game when playing with Cousins.

Without him, those averages dropped to 75.6 receiving yards and 0.39 touchdowns per game. That is a difference of more than 32 receiving yards per game.

Jefferson's 2026 numbers tell a similar story. Through eight games, Jefferson has recorded 31 receptions for 393 yards and four touchdowns. He is averaging 56.1 receiving yards per game, well below the standard he established during his best seasons.

Jefferson finished 2025 with 1,048 yards and two touchdowns, while his 2024 campaign produced 1,533 yards and 10 scores. In 2022, with Cousins throwing him the football, Jefferson exploded for 1,809 yards and eight touchdowns, leading the league in receiving yards.

Vikings explored different options before trading for Kirk Cousins

Minnesota's quarterback search reportedly extended beyond Cousins. Jordan Schultz reported that the Vikings also inquired about Justin Herbert, Daniel Jones and Geno Smith before completing the trade. The Los Angeles Chargers immediately shut down all inquiries about Herbert, while Minnesota ultimately landed on a quarterback who spent six seasons with the franchise.

According to Tom Pelissero of The Ringer , the Vikings sent their original 2027 third-round pick to the Raiders, but retained their first- and second-round selections, as well as the Philadelphia Eagles' third-round pick.

With a 6-2 record, the Vikings still had a decent shot at competing in the NFC. However, reuniting Jefferson with Cousins, who already has 2,340 yards and 20 touchdowns this season, has made Kevin O'Connell's team a legitimate contender.

Because for me, that's one of the most important things," Jones said. "It's the heart. So when we look at the Padres acquisition, how do we continue to build these bridges and unify?"

articles.title: NFL trade deadline 2026: Denver Broncos latest news and rumors
articles.summary: Here are all of the NFL trade deadline news and rumors surrounding our Denver Broncos. The deadline is Tuesday, November 10th at 2pm mountain.
articles.body:
The NFL trade deadline is Tuesday, November 10th at 2 p.m. MT, and our Denver Broncos could be an active team prior to the deadline. They have been widely connected to Colts star running back Jonathan Taylor in the days leading up to the deadline , but according to 9NEWS Denver's Mike Klis, the team could explore adding a weapon or two to their offense. He mentions running back, tight end, and wide receiver as the positions that they could add.

Looking at the Broncos' needs heading into the deadline, the most glaring one is running back. Now, the emergence of rookie running back Jonah Coleman helps, but the Broncos still need more from the position. RJ Harvey and Tyler Badie are on the injured reserve, and veteran JK Dobbins has been struggling all season. So, adding another back to pair with Coleman would make sense.

The question is, will they go big and add a Jonathan Taylor or Breece Hall? Or make a smaller move for someone like Tony Pollard or someone else?

Klis mentions wide receiver, and while it may not be the most pressing need right now, it could be in a few months. Jaylen Waddle has not performed as expected thus far; Courtland Sutton will be 32 next season and has a large cap hit(Also restructured his deal and could be off the team next season); Pat Bryant has been very good, but has been on the IR; Marvin Mims is a pending free agent, while Troy Franklin is buried on the depth chart. Could the Broncos be looking to add a wide receiver who could contribute to this team this season and moving forward? This doesn't seem as likely, but I wouldn't rule it out if the right deal comes their way.

As for tight end, I don't know. The only name that could move the needle and that might be available is Dallas Goedert, but is that even worth it? He would certainly improve that room, but the Broncos really do not utilize their tight ends in the passing game. Evan Engram has had a disappointing year, and blocking specialist Nate Adkins leads the group (and, funny enough, the team) in TD receptions with 3, but he only has 6 total catches thus far.

We'll be tracking all the Broncos news and rumors throughout the weekend and right up to the deadline. It's supposed to be an active deadline, so we'll see if our Denver Broncos make any splashes or not in the coming days.

articles.title: UCLA is 6-6 all-time against Illinois entering the Week 11 matchup
articles.summary: The UCLA Bruins are set to host the Illinois Fighting Illini Friday night at the Rose Bowl. The two teams are 6-6 all-time.
articles.body:
Friday night's meeting between the UCLA Bruins and the Illinois Fighting Illini may be the first time that the two schools are squaring off as Big Ten Conference opponents, but the two programs have faced off a dozen times over the past 79 years.

Currently, UCLA and Illinois are deadlocked at 6-6 with this week's game set to give one program some bragging rights.

None of the UCLA-Illinois meetings have been recent, with the last one taking place in 2011 at the Kraft Fight Hunger Bowl at AT&T Park (Now Oracle Park) in San Francisco. Illinois grabbed a 20-14 win against interim UCLA head coach Mike Johnson, who took over for the fired Rick Neuheisel .

The last time UCLA defeated Illinois was back in 2004 in a nonconference game where Maurice Jones-Drew, Marcedes Lewis and Craig Bragg led the Bruin offense in a 35-17 road win. UCLA and Illinois played each other in 2003 and 2004, with the Bruins winning both games. In 2003, the Bruins held on for a 6-3 win at the Rose Bowl where UCLA won the game despite totaling just 204 yards of offense.

Before that Illinois and UCLA clashed in a pair of bowl games over the course of the 1980s and 1990s, with UCLA getting wins in the 1991 John Hancock Bowl and the 1984 Rose Bowl. It was a blowout in the Rose Bowl, with Rick Neuheisel winning MVP of the 45-9 game. Illinois kept things closer in the John Hancock Bowl, with the Bruins holding on for a 6-3 win, with linebacker Arnold Ale earning MVP in the game.

UCLA will look to stay perfect on the 2026 season and add some more recent success against Illinois Friday evening in Pasadena, with the Bruins entering the game as 10 point favorites.
