articles.title: NFL trade deadline deal tracker includes Jessie Bates, Kirk Cousins, and more
articles.summary: Tracking all the deals made ahead of the NFL’s trade deadline
articles.body:
The 2026 NFL trade deadline is right around the corner. Teams have until 4:00 p.m. Eastern Time on Tuesday, November 10, to make deals in an effort to either improve rosters for a playoff push, or prepare for a rebuild over the upcoming offseason.

But some teams have not waited to push deals across the line.

Monday began with the news that the Atlanta Falcons were sending defensive back Jessie Bates III to the Jacksonville Jaguars, as general manager James Gladstone tries to improve a defense that is already considered one of the best in the league.

While we expect more deals to come, here is a running list of the trades that have gone down so far. This will be updated as new deals come through.

Indianapolis is trading wide receiver Josh Downs to the Kansas City Chiefs, giving Patrick Mahomes another target in the passing game.

Chiefs receive: WR Josh Downs and a 2027 seventh-round pick

Colts receive: A 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2027 fifth-round pick

The Broncos are adding on defense, acquiring linebacker Daiyan Henley from the Los Angeles Chargers in the rare trade between division rivals.

Chargers receive: A 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick

After a poor showing on "Monday Night Football," the Minnesota Vikings are trading for Kirk Cousins. The move brings Cousins back to Minnesota, reuniting him with Kevin O'Connell. It also paves the way for the start of the Fernando Mendoza era in Las Vegas.

Raiders receive: A 2027 third-round pick.

A defense that could use some help is getting it.

The Tennessee Titans, having already traded Jeffery Simmons to the Bears, are sending safety Amani Hooker to the Buffalo Bills.

Bills receive: S Amani Hooker and a 2027 fifth-round pick

Titans receive: A 2027 second-round pick

The trades are back on the docket in Indianapolis.

After reportedly hitting the pause button over the weekend, the Colts are back in the headlines. Indianapolis is sending veteran wide receiver Keenan Allen to the San Francisco 49ers, a team that has been hampered by injuries at that position.

The Eagles are not done making moves. On Tuesday, Philadelphia traded pass rusher Arnold Ebiketie to the Cincinnati Bengals, giving the AFC North contenders another presence on the edge.

The Jacksonville Jaguars are absolutely all-in on the 2026 season.

After acquiring both Jessie Bates III and Davon Godchaux earlier in the day, James Gladstone added yet another piece, trading for defensive tackle Jordan Davis in a deal with the Philadelphia Eagles.

Davis has tallied 31 tackles and 1.5 sacks this season, including a sack of J.J. McCarthy on Sunday in Philadelphia's 19-11 loss to the New York Giants. The trade gives Anthony Campanile yet another talented player on the interior, and now Eagles general manager Howie Roseman has a pair of picks in the first round of the 2027 NFL Draft.

Eagles receive: A 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick

The Detroit Lions are getting some help on defense.

The New York Jets are trading safety Andre Cisco to Detroit. The safety is on an expiring contract, and the Jets — who at the moment have more than $80 million in available cap space for next year — are getting what they can now.

Jets receive: A 2028 sixth-round selection

The Jacksonville Jaguars are not done adding to their defense.

Hours after trading for safety Jessie Bates III, the Jaguars swung a deal with the New Orleans Saints to acquire defensive tackle Davon Godchaux. While Bates can patrol the deep third of the defense and gives defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile a flexible safety that can play both in the deep middle and down near that line of scrimmage, Godchaux gives Jacksonville another option along the defensive line. That is something the Jaguars needed to add after the team lost DaVon Hamilton for the season due to a torn quad.

Saints receive: 2028 sixth-round pick ( which could elevate to a 2027 sixth-round pick if Jacksonville acquires one via trade or the compensatory selection formula)

Falcons trade Jessie Bates III to Jaguars

Trade deadline week kicked off in style with the Atlanta Falcons sending veteran safety Jessie Bates III to the Jacksonville Jaguars. For the Jaguars, it is a move to shore up the secondary as Jacksonville tries to maximize the current window of contention. For Atlanta, it is a move to get something for Bates ahead of his free agency, and with the Falcons currently looking at over $100 million in cap space, they might not receive a compensatory selection for Bates should he walk in free agency and Atlanta make the most of those resources.

Falcons receive: A 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick

Cardinals trade Jacoby Brissett to Ravens

With Arizona benching quarterback Jacoby Brissett, and the Ravens suddenly looking at life without Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley for at least the next few weeks as both are dealing with injuries, this move makes a good bit of sense. Brissett gets a chance to play on a team that is trying to stay in the playoff chase, the Ravens get a quarterback that gives them a chance to do just that, and Arizona … well maybe they could have handled things differently but they got some picks in return.

Ravens receive: QB Jacoby Brissett and a 2027 fifth-round pick

Cardinals receive: A 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 seventh-round pick

With the Chicago Bears trying to keep pace in the tough NFC North, and the defense remaining an issue, general manager Ryan Poles swung for the fences, bringing in defensive lineman Jeffery Simmons in a trade with the Tennessee Titans. Simmons paid immediate dividends, as he was stellar in his Chicago debut against the Seattle Seahawks.

Bears receive: DL Jeffery Simmons and a 2028 fifth-round pick

Titans receive: A 2027 first-round pick, a 2028 first-round pick, and a 2027 fourth-round pick

After parting ways with general manager Chris Ballard, the Colts began moving players with an eye to the future. One of those deals saw Indianapolis send DeForest Buckner back to the San Francisco 49ers, returning the defensive lineman to the team that drafted him with the seventh-overall pick in the 2016 NFL Draft.

Indianapolis started their impending fire sale with a move involving guard Quenton Nelson. Still one of the premier interior offensive linemen in the NFL, the Colts sent him to Seattle as the Seahawks look to shore up their offensive line.

Colts receive: A 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick

Cardinals trade Marvin Harrison Jr. to Texans

It just never seemed to click for Marvin Harrison Jr. in Arizona.

Billed as one of the top wide receiver prospects in recent memory, Harrison never quite lived up to that hype with the Cardinals. Arizona selected him as the fourth-overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft, and after catching 62 passes for 885 yards and eight touchdowns as a rookie, he caught just 41 passes during 2025 and had only pulled in five receptions through the first four games of the season with Arizona.

In a move that reunited him with former college teammate C.J. Stroud, the Texans acquired him to try and give Stroud a familiar target in the passing game.

Texans receive: WR Marvin Harrison Jr. and a 2027 sixth-round pick

Cardinals receive: A 2027 second-round pick and a 2027 seventh-round pick

Back at the start of October, the Baltimore Ravens swung a deal for offensive lineman Cam Jurgens of the Eagles.

The move was made to shore up the interior offensive line, in the wake of center Tyler Linderbaum signing with the Las Vegas Raiders last offseason. Baltimore's top three centers were on injured reserve at the time the move was made, and the Ravens were using rookie guard Olaivavega Ioane in the middle.

Ravens receive: IOL Cam Jurgens and a 2027 seventh-round pick

Eagles receive: A 2027 fifth-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick

Steelers trade Joey Porter Jr. to Cowboys

October began with the Pittsburgh Steelers finally coming to a decision on cornerback Joey Porter Jr. Porter was seeking a contract extension from the team, but the two sides were unable to come to terms on a new deal. He also missed each of Pittsburgh's first three games of the season due to a lingering back injury.

So Jerry Jones stepped in, acquiring the cornerback in yet another move to try and shore up a struggling defense.

Steelers receive: A 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick

The first big trade of the 2026 NFL season came back at the end of September.

When the New York Giants lost quarterback Jaxson Dart to a knee injury, many wondered if the team would swing a trade for a quarterback.

Enter J.J. McCarthy. With the former Michigan passer on the losing end of a camp battle with Kyler Murray — and relegated to the QB3 spot to begin the year behind Carson Wentz — he found a fresh start in the Big Apple. And he has taken over as the team's starting quarterback, leading the Giants to wins over Houston and Philadelphia over the past two games.

Vikings receive: A 2027 fifth-round pick

articles.title: Mariners Are Most Obvious Team for Red Sox to Make Blockbuster Trade With
articles.summary: With the arms the Mariners have and the bats the Red Sox have, it's a perfect match.
articles.body:
With the Boston Red Sox expected to have some needs on the mound, and Sonny Gray expected to depart in free agency, the front office has a few ways to approach this winter.

There are a couple of decent starting pitchers out there, but outside of Tarik Skubal, there isn't exactly a lights-out pitcher on this free agency market.

There are a couple of intriguing names on the potential trade market, however, with the Seattle Mariners having two of them.

It would be questionable for the Mariners to move on from George Kirby or Emerson Hancock, but Seattle has other needs in the offense and could be willing to trade some of those guys for the right package.

Whether it would be Seattle getting prospects back or big league talent is one thing, but either way, the Red Sox could be of interest to both of those teams.

"The Red Sox built their team on pitching and defense, and they shouldn't go away from that plan in 2027 just because they need to upgrade the offense. The Seattle Mariners have multiple starting pitchers with at least two years of team control that they are willing to listen on. Acquiring one to add to Garrett Crochet, Payton Tolle, and Ranger Suarez would be one of the best rotations in baseball.

"The Mariners reportedly want to use one of their pitchers to find an impact bat for their lineup. Breslow could kill two birds with one stone by using one of the outfielders to give them just that. The Red Sox can't go into 2027 with the amount of uncertainty in the bottom two of the rotation they currently have, and getting one of the Mariners' starters would be an excellent long-term fix to that situation," Brian Burrows wrote .

As Burrows noted, the Mariners looking for an offensive player who can come in and help immediately would give the Red Sox multiple options to move on from. Even if they wanted to go the prospect route, there are a few prospects in the Red Sox system who can help out Seattle in the short and long term.

For Boston, the bigger thing here would be getting one of these two guys who have elite stuff. Kirby is coming off a season in which he struggled, posting a 4.33 ERA.

However, if he can get back to his 2023 and 2024 form, there's reason to believe he can be an elite arm in this Red Sox rotation, especially since he's still just 28.

articles.title: Santi Aldama Fixes Dallas Offense After Brutal Losses
articles.summary: Santi Aldama's return sparked a massive Mavericks turnaround. See how his rebounding and shooting solved Dallas' biggest offensive holes.
articles.body:
The Dallas Mavericks finally found their rhythm on Sunday night, crushing the Brooklyn Nets by a staggering 37-point margin. This 130-93 victory marks the team's largest winning streak of the season so far. Following a slump marked by consecutive defeats against the Sacramento Kings and San Antonio Spurs, the victory arrives. Per The Smoking Cuban , this sharp turnaround coincides directly with the return of Santi Aldama to the starting lineup.

Aldama is filling a roster spot and solving specific problems that plagued the offense all year. The team struggled mightily in their last game against Utah, shooting just 41.9 percent from the field and a poor 28.1 percent from three-point range. However, the energy shifted instantly when Aldama got back on the court. According to The Smoking Cuban , the Mavericks have improved considerably in offensive rebounding and second-chance points specifically because of his presence.

For a long time, Dallas could not secure loose balls near the rim. Throughout the whole league last year, the squad placed 22nd for offensive rebounding and 24th for second-chance points. One year prior, the Mavericks ranked among the NBA's poorest scoring teams after a missed shot. That stat line has flipped in a hurry. Against the Utah Jazz, Dallas outrebounded the opponent 21-8 on the offensive glass. This dominance led to a massive 21-5 advantage in second-chance points. Aldama alone grabbed nine rebounds in that game, with four of them coming on the offensive end.

The big man's size alone gives Dallas a bonus that other teams cannot match. He is not pigeonholed into playing only center or power forward, which changes how the offense flows. His shooting skill enables Aldama to occupy the three position, He played even when paired with Morez Johnson Jr. in lineups and Daniel Gafford. His perimeter game was on full display against Brooklyn, where he scored 12 points. He shot 5-of-7 from the floor and hit 2-of-4 from three-point range. Aldama scored in a variety of ways, including a basket off a dribble drive that showed his unique skill set.

The length and versatility Aldama brings have already stood out in these recent wins. The 7-foot big man helps the team handle defensive pressure and creates easy looks for teammates. His ability to stretch the floor opens up driving lanes for guards who were previously clogged. The improvement in both rebounding and scoring options suggests the team is only getting better. Per The Smoking Cuban, Aldama is a key reason the Mavericks are now two games above .500.

articles.title: Colts sign WR Nick Westbrook-Ikhine from the practice squad
articles.summary: The Colts signed wide receiver Nick Westbrook-Ikhine to the 53-player roster from the practice squad, the team announced.
articles.body:
The Colts signed wide receiver Nick Westbrook-Ikhine to the 53-player roster from the practice squad, the team announced.

They also announced they signed long snapper Jacob Bobenmoyer to the practice squad.

Westbrook-Ikhine originally signed with the team as a free agent on March 18. He was cut out of the preseason and signed back to the team's practice squad on Aug. 31.

He has played three games this season, so he was out of elevations.

Westbrook-Ikhine has played 96 career games with 42 starts in his time with the Colts (2026), Dolphins (2025) and Titans (2020-24). He has totaled 137 receptions for 1,862 yards and 19 touchdowns.

Bobenmoyer has appeared in 98 career games in his time with the Jaguars (2026), Raiders (2023-25) and Broncos (2020-22). He has compiled 22 special teams tackles and one fumble recovery.

articles.title: 😳 384 logos on one shirt? Club plans craziest stunt ever
articles.summary: Why have one big main sponsor when you can have 384 (!)? Yes, you read that right: Brazilian club São Joseense, from the state of Paraná, is flipping the scr...
articles.body:
Why have one big main sponsor when you can have 384 (!)? Yes, you read that right: Brazilian club São Joseense, from the state of Paraná, is flipping the script for the 2027 season. Instead of signing a single mega-deal, the club is turning its new shirt into a colorful mosaic for the local community, with a whopping 384 advertising spaces.

Each advertising space measures a compact 3.5 by 3.5 centimeters. Depending on whether the logo takes pride of place on the chest or ends up nearer the hem, interested sponsors will pay between 2,000 and 15,000 reais (roughly €300 to €2,500).

But what is the club hoping to achieve? According to a press release, the aim is to give small businesses the chance to buy advertising space on the club's shirt. "Being a main sponsor costs a lot of money, which severely limits who can get involved. Our shirt project now gives microbusiness owners and sports enthusiasts an affordable way in," explained Eduardo Grassi.

The club's managing director also emphasized: "We want business owners and fans to feel part of this sporting journey—in a city that lives and breathes football but has until now lacked a team of its own to identify with. This is another step toward making São Joseense more prominent and better equipped for a year full of sporting challenges awaiting us in 2027." Among other things, the club will make its debut in the prestigious Brazilian cup competition, the Copa do Brasil.

For the mini-sponsors, that means exposure and TV airtime that microbusinesses can usually only dream of.

Once the design is finalized, the shirts may well look like a giant QR code from a distance. But in the stands and among local businesses, the initiative is probably already creating exactly what every club hopes for: the feeling of being out on the pitch together.

articles.title: Colts sign wide receiver to roster after Allen, Downs trades
articles.summary: After trading Josh Downs and Keenan Allen, the Colts made a wide receiver addition to the 53-man roster.
articles.body:
After trading Keenan Allen to the San Francisco 49ers and Josh Downs to the Kansas City Chiefs, the Indianapolis Colts announced an addition at the wide receiver position.

To bolster their receiver depth on the 53-man, Nick Westbrook-Ikhine is being signed from the practice squad to the active roster.

Westbrook-Ikhine was signed by the Colts in free agency and was eventually released during roster cutdowns. He has spent the season up to this point on the practice squad.

Westbrook-Ikhine has appeared in three games this season as a practice squad elevation. He's played just 19 offensive snaps, with only one target coming his way. His primary role in these games has been on special teams, where he's played 45 snaps.

The Colts also announced that they signed veteran long-snapper Jake Bobenmoyer to the practice squad.

As Mike Chappell noted, Luke Rhodes may be dealing with something.

articles.title: Big Ten football coach to reportedly return next season amid firing speculation
articles.summary: A Big Ten coach that was considered to be on the hot seat will reportedly be retained for next season
articles.body:
A Big Ten football coach has been given a vote of confidence and will reportedly be returning for next season despite speculation of an upcoming dismissal.

While there were some who thought this would be the end of the road for Greg Schiano at Rutgers, that is not the case. Pete Thamel of ESPN reported on Tuesday that Rutgers plans to retain Schiano for another season, which will be his 19th as head coach of the Scarlet Knights .

Rutgers would have had to pay Schiano nearly $19 million in his buyout should they had decided to fire him this year.

Rutgers is in the midst of a tough season, currently sitting at 2-7 overall and 1-5 in Big Ten play. The Scarlet Knights opened the season with a disappointing home loss to UMass, which got the chatter going if this would be Schiano's final year at Rutgers.

Michigan State will end the regular season at Rutgers on November 28. That road game for the Spartans could end up being important for bowl eligibility if Michigan State is able to win each of its next two games against Washington and Oregon.

articles.title: Chargers trade LB Daiyan Henley to Broncos for ‘27 4th, ‘28 5th
articles.summary: The Chargers are trading LB Daiyan Henley to the Broncos for a 4th and 5th round pick.
articles.body:
The Chargers ended up trading away one of their players after all.

Per several NFL insiders, the Bolts are sending linebacker Daiyan Henley to the Denver Broncos for a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick. Henley was originally a third-round pick back in 2023 out of Washington State and has been the team's starting middle linebacker since the 2024 season.

Henley is also a team captain and the "green dot" player who calls the defense for the Chargers. At the same time, Henley is currently in the final deal of his rookie contract and no real attempts at an extension had ever come to the table. It's going to be a rough scene in that locker room as Henley has also been one of the most beloved players on the entire team during his young career.

Through the team's eight games this season, Henley has been their leading tackler with 51. He has also posted two tackles for loss, a half sack, two pass breakups, an interception, a forced fumble, and two fumble recoveries.

He now joins former Chargers running back JK Dobbins in Denver.

articles.title: Chiefs agree to trade for WR Josh Downs
articles.summary: Josh Downs has gotten his wish.
articles.body:
After requesting a trade from the Colts, the Chiefs have agreed to acquire the wide receiver, according to multiple reports.

Kansas City will receive Downs and a 2027 seventh-round pick in exchange for 2027 fourth- and fifth-round picks.

Downs, who is in his fourth season, has caught 33 passes for 354 yards with an interception so far in 2026. He had 58 catches for 566 yards with four touchdowns in 16 games last year.

A third-round pick in the 2023 draft, Downs has recorded 231 career catches for 2,494 yards with 12 touchdowns in his 56 games.

The Chiefs have been looking for more depth at receiver and now have a new weapon in Downs. He could also play 18 games, as the Chiefs have already had their bye while the Colts don't have theirs until Week 13.

articles.title: Kyle Busch’s Hauler Drives Away For The Final Time At Homestead
articles.summary: The No. 8 hauler leaves Homestead-Miami Speedway for the last time after Kyle Busch's tragic death. See the emotional tribute that ended the 2026 season.
articles.body:
The No. 8 hauler left Homestead-Miami Speedway on Sunday night for the very last time, marking a somber end to the 2026 NASCAR Cup Series season. After the championship race concluded, the 1.5-mile track was exited by this massive truck, which bore the signature of the late Kyle Busch, as it drove through the tunnel. Fans watched a video by Motorsport showing the team loading up the equipment out of deep respect for the driver who won 234 races across the top three series before his sudden death in May.

Austin Hill took over the ride for Richard Childress Racing, piloting the No. 33 Chevrolet to a 15th-place finish in the finale. The team changed the car number from 8 to 33 to honor Busch, yet they kept the old hauler on site until this final departure. In 2027, Hill is scheduled to return full-time to the No. 33, shouldering a season marked by both a championship and a tragedy. His best effort this year came at Talladega with a 14th-place result, but Sunday was about saying goodbye.

The 2026 season will forever be remembered for two Kyles: Kyle Larson's dominant playoff surge and Kyle Busch's shocking death. Larson clinched his third Cup Series title during the opening stage of the finale, finishing 12th at Homestead-Miami Speedway to cap a 49-point victory over Christopher Bell. Even though Larson became the 11th driver in history to win three titles, he refused to look back at his achievements while the sport mourned.

"I just feel like when you're in it and you're competing, it's just so hard to reflect in the moment," Larson said, according to a report . He added that he still has more to accomplish and plans to keep looking out the windshield rather than stopping to admire the rearview mirror. The championship celebration at the annual awards banquet on Tuesday will likely name Busch the most popular driver, honoring a man who died after severe pneumonia progressed into sepsis.

NASCAR leadership made sure the memory of "Rowdy" stayed front and center during the final race. Every fan in the grandstands received a No. 8 Busch flag, and a memorial graphic dedicated to him was painted directly on the frontstretch. The NBC TV booth observed a silent Lap 8 in his honor, with many attendees holding up eight fingers to pay tribute to the two-time champion.

"It's tough to not talk about Kyle when you're back in Miami," NASCAR CEO Steve O'Donnell said. He described Busch as an extraordinary competitor who won the championship at this very track and left a forever mark on the sport. O'Donnell admitted that celebrating a championship feels different without him, noting that the community still misses him deeply. Busch won both of his Cup titles in 2015 and 2019 at Homestead, making his final farewell at this venue even more poignant.

articles.title: Shawn Horcoff Addresses the Dylan Larkin Trade Standoff
articles.summary: Shawn Horcoff addressed the Dylan Larkin standoff in Toronto, and Simon Edvinsson's signing clock is running. #RedWings
articles.body:
Detroit Red Wings interim general manager Shawn Horcoff met with reporters at the NHL general managers' meetings in Toronto on Tuesday, and nothing he said moved either of the two situations hanging over his roster. Asked about the Dylan Larkin trade standoff and Simon Edvinsson's unsigned contract, Horcoff said it was "status quo" with both players.

Horcoff declined to comment on Dylan Larkin's trade list

The one detail that would tell everyone how close this is to ending stayed off the table. Nicholas J. Cotsonika of NHL.com reported that "Horcoff declined to comment on whether Larkin has altered the list of teams to which he would agree to be traded."

Horcoff did describe what a resolution has to look like from Detroit's side. "Ideally, we get something that works for both sides, right?" he said . "But it has to be something that helps this team."

Larkin still has only 10 teams on his list

The Red Wings would like Larkin to open up his approved list, and so far it has not changed. TSN's Pierre LeBrun reported that Detroit has exhausted its options with the current 10 teams and would like to go deeper in talks with six to eight clubs outside them, while Larkin's camp believes the list is already long enough. As long as it stays at 10, the market Detroit can actually work is small.

Per LeBrun, the 10 teams are the New Jersey Devils, the Colorado Avalanche, the Vegas Golden Knights, the Dallas Stars, the Minnesota Wild, the Washington Capitals, the Utah Mammoth, the Carolina Hurricanes, the Tampa Bay Lightning and the Florida Panthers. Larkin is suspended without pay for now, which means Horcoff and the Red Wings can take their time with a trade.

The 30-year-old center has played in 10 games this season for the Red Wings. Larkin scored two goals and recorded four assists with a plus-3 rating, according to ESPN .

Horcoff still wants to sign Simon Edvinsson

The other half of the status quo carries a hard date. Edvinsson, 23, is an unsigned restricted free agent working out in Nashville, and Cotsonika reported that the defenseman must sign by Dec. 1 to be eligible to play this season.

Horcoff has said he has no interest in trading Edvinsson, and on Tuesday he did not close the door on listening. "I'd still like to sign Simon, but I think when it's someone like that and the situation that we're in, you can't help but take calls," Horcoff said. He added that his job is to do what is in the best interest of the Red Wings, and that he will take those calls and hear what other teams have to say.

The Gators (5-4) are projected to face Arizona in the Las Vegas Bowl on Dec. 31, according to Erick Smith's latest bowl projections released Tuesday.

Florida was previously projected to face Louisville in the Gator Bowl, but Saturday's 23-7 loss to Oklahoma has complicated its postseason outlook. Smith now has Clemson facing Oklahoma in the Gator Bowl on Dec. 30, while Louisville is projected to meet Houston in the Pop-Tarts Bowl.

The Las Vegas Bowl features an SEC representative against a Pac-12-affiliated opponent, with legacy Pac-12 schools continuing to fulfill existing bowl agreements through the 2026 season. Arizona, now a member of the Big 12, remains eligible for those arrangements.

The Wildcats enter the contest at 7-2 after suffering a 34-6 loss to Tennessee last weekend. Florida will also face Tennessee and Florida State before the regular season concludes.

Although the Gators have not yet secured bowl eligibility, Smith's latest projections suggest Florida could still extend its postseason streak despite an inconsistent first season under Sumrall.

articles.title: Why Chiefs are reportedly trading two picks for Colts WR Josh Downs
articles.summary: The Chiefs are making a much-needed addition to the WR room on deadline day.
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs came into NFL trade deadline day with one very simple goal: acquire a wide receiver to help the offense.

While Keenan Allen was dealt to the San Francisco 49ers , there was a different wide receiver from the Indianapolis Colts that they've had their eye on. Finally, with under half an hour to go, they made their move.

According to Tom Pelissero of The Ringer , the Chiefs are making a move for Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Josh Downs. In exchange for a pair of picks, the Chiefs are getting a new WR for Patrick Mahomes.

Why Chiefs are trading for Josh Downs from Colts

"Trade! The Chiefs are acquiring WR Josh Downs and a 2027 seventh-round pick from the Colts for a 2027 fourth-round and fifth-round picks, sources tell @ringer @netflixsports," Pelissero reports.

Downs is a rental wide receiver for the Chiefs who instantly provides another solid weapon in the passing game for this offense.

He'll join Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy in Kansas City, with running back Kenneth Walker III and tight end Travis Kelce making up a strong offensive supporting cast for Mahomes.

The Chiefs are making this trade thanks in large part to Tyquan Thornton's season-ending injury. Add in that Worthy is banged up and has been underwhelming, and a WR addition was a must-have for this team.

A fourth-rounder and a fifth-rounder are a lot to give up for Downs for half a season and a seventh-round pick, but considering their major WR need and the other available options, this is a reasonable move for the Chiefs.

Kansas City desperately needed WR help, and Downs might be the best WR traded in the middle of the 2026 season. Marvin Harrison Jr. went for a second-round pick and hasn't been great for the Houston Texans .

The Chiefs, meanwhile, take a chance on Downs, who was having a down season with the Colts and their struggling offense.

This move shouldn't come as a surprise to anyone, as the Chiefs were strongly implied as the favorites, and now, they're reportedly adding him in a huge move at the trade deadline.

articles.title: Who will call plays for Oregon after Mehringer's firing?
articles.summary: Offensive assistant Jay Johnson will take over play-calling duties after Oregon fired coordinator Drew Mehringer following a three-game stretch where the Duc...
articles.body:
EUGENE — After firing first-year offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer seven games into the 2026 season, Dan Lanning shared Oregon 's plans for filling his role moving forward at his weekly press conference Monday night.

Offensive assistant Jay Johnson will lead offensive playcalling for the Ducks going forward, Lanning said.

"He has a lot of experience as a play-caller, was with me in Georgia when we were part of the national championship team," Lanning said. "Went on to have a lot of success in Colorado and Michigan State. He's gonna lead the efforts there with the offensive staff, but it'll still be a collaborative effort, with a lot of the work that we do.

"He's also coming in with a different perspective, a different view, not being with us the last few years, where he can provide a couple things that might be different than what we've done."

Mehringer, previously the tight ends coach for the Ducks, is the first assistant coach Lanning has fired in his tenure at Oregon, which began in 2022. The Ducks' offensive decision-making was at the center of intense criticism over the past three weeks, during which Oregon averaged just 14 points per game and lost twice to UCLA and Illinois.

Lanning spoke to the human element of letting Mehringer go.

"They see the football coach, right? That's also an unbelievable dad. A great husband," Lanning said. "The guy's been part of our staff for the last five years, that's done some really good things here, and I think all of us feel like we shoulder some of the blame. Because we didn't create success for our team this season."

articles.title: Video catches USC announcer's take on targeting call
articles.summary: USC radio announcer Pete Arbogast drew criticism for disputing a targeting call on Oregon QB Dante Moore, who suffered a concussion after a hit by USC lineba...
articles.body:
That's what many were asking regarding longtime USC football radio play-by-play announcer Pete Arbogast's reaction to Oregon quarterback Dante Moore being knocked out of Saturday's 41-27 Ducks ' victory at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum.

The play occurred in the second quarter when Moore scrambled and slid. USC linebacker Desman Stephens II then put his shoulder into Moore's head, knocking him backward into the turf.

Moore lay on the field for several minutes before being taken off on a cart and loaded into an ambulance.

Stephens celebrated the hit even after being flagged, leading to a skirmish with several Oregon players.

Meanwhile, up in the radio booth, Arbogast said the play did not appear to be targeting and claimed Moore didn't slide feet-first.

Arbogast went on to claim that Stephens went in helmet first and ran into Moore who "ducked into that hit."

"I saw him dive forward," Arbogast claimed.

Radio analyst Shaun Cody, who played defensive line at USC (2001-2004) and spent eight seasons in the NFL (Detroit and Houston ), clearly disagreed.

"He's laying feet first," Cody responded.

But Arbogast countered, "Well, he is now because they spun him around."

Cody disagreed again, and Arbogast said he wanted to see the replay, which clearly showed Moore sliding feet-first and Stephens going in head-first, with his right shoulder striking Moore in the head.

"Yeah, not a feet-first slide, it's more of a knee slide," Arbogast claimed while watching the replay.

While it's one thing not to see clearly a live play from high up in a radio booth, it's another to watch the replay and claim to see something that didn't exist.

Cody immediately smirked at Arbogast's viewpoint; then Arbogast added, "It didn't look like targeting on the replay to us."

In response, Cody looked directly into the camera, eyes wide, and nodded, clearly disagreeing with Arbogast's assessment.

Homerism? Maybe. Potential advertising fodder for local optometrists to encourage thousands to update their eyeglass prescriptions? Absolutely.

Oregon backup quarterback Dylan Raiola replaced Moore and passed for 289 yards and two touchdowns in the win.

Moore was later diagnosed with a concussion; he has entered concussion protocol and will be out indefinitely . Moore released a statement saying he would soon return.

articles.title: Damian Lillard is back and Ja Morant is here. How exactly is this going to work? | Bill Oram
articles.summary: The Blazers may have the most talented glut of point guards in NBA history. Does that make them any more of a threat in the Western Conference?
articles.body:
In the history of basketball, we have certainly seen some why-would-they-do-that? pairings.

Jerseys and sleeves. Kawhi Leonard and a tree sponsorship. Utah and "the Jazz."

Once, there was even Detlef Schrempf and a headband, if you can believe that.

We're about to find out if they belong on such a list.

Because of all the things you might have said the Trail Blazers needed as they prepared to welcome Lillard back after making a playoff run without him, a slight-of-stature ball-dominant guard with a questionable jump shot would not have topped anyone's list.

Depth on the wing? Yes. Shooting? Definitely. Defense? Always.

Morant doesn't particularly address any of those, and yet, he's here, a dynamic two-time All-Star in need of a second act, being paid a team-high $42.1 million to play the same position as not just Lillard, but Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson.

Heck, the Blazers' most valuable point guard last season was forward Deni Avdija.

"I'm sure there will be questions about fit," General Manager Joe Cronin said Monday.

The Blazers have little more than three weeks before the regular season begins in which to figure that out. At the team's annual media day on Monday, Morant appeared in a fresh white No. 1 Trail Blazers jersey. It's happening.

"It's easy for people to be like, 'Man how is this going to work,'" Lillard offered. "'They can't do this, they can't do that.' But being on the floor with them … we can be a dangerous team and I really believe that."

The onus is on the Trail Blazers starting this month to prove that they bet right in acquiring Morant. And that pairing him with Lillard isn't the boondoggle conventional wisdom suggests it will be.

Lillard noted how many teams that succeeded in the playoffs last year, think San Antonio with its four point guards, relied on numerous playmakers. To his credit, Morant said he would be comfortable coming off the bench, if necessary.

But they would not be the first NBA team to fall into the trap of believing they are capable of adjusting or that they will be comfortable sacrificing. It isn't uncommon to see players in those situations default to familiar habits and sensibilities once the season is underway or struggles come.

That's what made a lot of the positive energy around what sure seems like an awkward roster ring so hollow. We're going to need to see it to believe it.

Morant tried to lay out a vision for how it could look. If he drives to the paint and is double-teamed, someone else is inevitably open. That's how basketball works.

"That allows me to have more space to be the best Ja I can be," Morant said.

The 36-year-old Holiday, who would be a more natural complement next to Lillard or Morant than they are to each other, made his own case for why the point guard rotation makes sense.

"It's about being a complete basketball player for myself," he said, "and I think we have a lot of guys like that."

There is a long history of teams talking themselves into superstar additions that make little sense. The Los Angeles Lakers once made a conscious decision to acquire Russell Westbrook and pair him with LeBron James. Nobody made them do that!

The talent and star power of a Lillard-Morant backcourt is undeniable. Still, I remain unconvinced that Cronin, with a very hands-on new owner in his ear, made the deal with winning basketball games at the front of mind.

Although, admittedly, Cronin's biggest wins as a GM have been in the trade market.

The haul of assets he collected for Lillard, only to get him back two years later, will go down as an all-time great swindle. So, too, will the oft-questioned Avdija trade a year later.

Maybe he sees something in a Lillard-Morant pairing that many of us can't.

Morant could return to the All-Star form he had achieved before injuries and off-court issues derailed his ascent . And if he does, the Blazers can either trade him for pieces that fit better or clear out the logjam and build around him.

But to sell the current roster as a basketball strategy doesn't quite pass the smell test.

Neither Lillard nor Morant has achieved stardom due to his defensive acumen. Each player needs the ball in his hands to thrive. If the duo is on the floor together, Avdija is no longer the secondary playmaker, he becomes tertiary.

So, you are left to wonder whether the Blazers sold themselves on Morant because of how he can help the current collection of talent or if they simply saw the opportunity to land a 27-year-old All-NBA talent for cheap, regardless of what it meant for the existing roster construction.

And if you're being honest, you probably don't need to wonder which of the two it is.

"We were very focused and we'll continue to be on … adding to our talent base as much as we can," Cronin said.

That thinking right there may tell you just how far ahead of everyone else the San Antonio Spurs and Oklahoma City Thunder are in the Western Conference. They are positioned to dominate for the next half-decade, if not longer. The only chance any other team has of disrupting that is taking bold risks.

But I thought the goal was to go all in on the twilight years of Lillard's career?

"Dame literally just wants to win," said first-year head coach Micah Nori, whose charge is to sort out arguably the most talented glut of point guard talent in NBA history. "I think that's the only thing left he really has to (do). He's already proven he's a winner, but at the highest level."

Does adding Morant move Lillard closer to a title? Or simply give Portland a potential off-ramp if Lillard is no longer the same player after tearing his Achilles tendon?

Morant was without question a low-risk, high-reward addition. He came at the reasonable price of Jerami Grant and Kris Murray. If it becomes clear that Morant is one point guard too many, or that he's just not the player he once was, some will argue that it didn't cost the Blazers much to try.

However, there is an opportunity cost to messing with Lillard's swan song. If you don't get it right, you risk wasting the gift of his voluntary return last summer . And, not for nothing, Lillard has the option to become a free agent again after this season.

The franchise icon certainly hasn't said anything that would suggest he is unhappy about Morant's presence, although he stopped short on Monday of a full-throated endorsement. He said he knew about the trade before it went through.

When I asked if he thought it was a good idea right away or if he needed time to get on board with the plan, Lillard said, "My position on it was, I'm prepared for whatever."

It's good that he's already thinking about other positions. Because his old one is getting awfully crowded.

articles.title: Land Rover acusa a la china BYD de copiar su Defender y la lleva a los tribunales
articles.standfirst: En pocos días habrá una resolución preliminar sobre si los chinos han violado la propiedad intelectual o industrial de la marca británica, más allá del parecido estético
articles.summary: En pocos días habrá una resolución preliminar sobre si los chinos han violado la propiedad intelectual o industrial de la marca británica, más allá del parecido estético
articles.body: Guerra a la vista entre Land Rover y BYD. La marca británica ha denunciado a la china acusándola de plagiar su modelo más icónico: el Defender. En concreto, Land Rover alude a uno de los modelos del fabricante asiático que está al a venta en China y acaba de aterrizar también en Europa, precisamente en el mercado británico: el Fangchenbao Ti7, que en nuestro continente se comercializará bajo la enseña BYD, también como Ti7. Según los británicos, el 4x4 chino no sólo se habría inspirado (o algo más) en la estética del Defender, para lo cual alude al parecido de la zona lateral, sobre todo de los paneles de la carrocería integrados en las ventanillas laterales traseras, sino que habría algo más. Land Rover considera que también hay plagio tecnológico, hasta el punto de que creen que la china ha hecho ingeniería inversa (es decir, habrían desmontado unidades del Defender para analizar algunos de sus aspectos técnicos que luego se habrían reproducido). Algo que no es ilegal de por sí, salvo que viole patentes y otros derechos de propiedad intelectual o industrial, en este caso de Land Rover. La denuncia, que ha salido a la luz ahora en la prensa británica, apenas unos pocos días antes de la primera vista preliminar, data de finales del verano y se ha concretrado en una operación judicial: el registro de las sedes de BYD en Schiedam y Hoofddorp (Holanda). El BYD Ti7 es un 4x4 de 5,06 metros, interior con siete plazas, propulsión híbrida enchufable con 354 caballos de potencia y un precio en el mercado británico inferior a los 60.000 euros... cuando el Land Rover Defender cuesta más de 80.000. A la espera de la decisión de los tribunales, hay que decir que no es la primera vez que Land Rover lleva a cabo un proceso judicial de este tipo. En 2016 hizo lo propio con Great Wall Motors (GWM), al denunciar plagio sobre el Landwind X7 (en este caso, una copia del Range Rover Evoque). En aquella ocasión la británica ganó el caso al considerar la justicia que el SUV chino copiaba cinco elementos distintivos del Evoque y condenó a GWM a detener su producción.

articles.title: Inspiring story of the day: “We just stay in our own little world” - How Tiger Woods turned his comeback into a fatherhood triumph with son Charlie Woods
articles.summary: Tiger Woods’ journey back to golf after his life-threatening 2021 car crash was about more than returning to competition.
articles.body: Tiger Woods’ journey back to golf after his life-threatening 2021 car crash was about more than returning to competition. The 15-time major champion had suffered serious injuries to his right leg, and doctors had to consider the possibility that he might lose it. Yet, one of his most meaningful moments after the accident came when he returned to the course with his son, Charlie Woods. Their relationship has since grown through junior tournaments, shared competitions and lessons that go beyond golf. For Tiger, being there for Charlie has become a different kind of victory.How did Tiger Woods choose a different path from his father, Earl Woods?Tiger Woods grew up under the strict guidance of his father, Earl Woods, who introduced him to golf when he was still a baby. Earl, a former Green Beret, believed in building mental strength through discipline and pressure. His approach helped shape Tiger into one of the most successful golfers in history, but Tiger’s own experience as a father has taken a different direction.When Charlie and his older sister, Sam Woods, were growing up, Tiger did not make golf a condition of their relationship with him. Charlie was allowed to enjoy other interests, including soccer, before developing a stronger interest in golf. Rather than deciding what his son should become, Tiger gave him room to find his own path.That difference has become important as Charlie’s golf career has developed. Tiger can share everything he has learned from decades at the highest level, but he has not tried to make his son’s career a copy of his own. Charlie has his own goals, competitions and decisions to make.Tiger also understands that having a famous father can bring pressure that other young players do not face. Every tournament Charlie enters attracts attention, and even ordinary mistakes can become a talking point. Allowing his son to learn through his own performances has therefore been an important part of their relationship.How did Tiger Woods return to golf after his 2021 car crash?On February 23, 2021, Tiger was involved in a serious single-car crash in Rancho Palos Verdes, California. The accident left him with multiple open fractures in the upper and lower parts of his right tibia and fibula, along with major injuries to his ankle and foot.Doctors inserted a rod into his tibia and used screws and pins to stabilise the damaged bones. The injuries were so serious that Tiger later revealed how close he had come to losing his leg. In a November 2021 interview with Golf Digest, he said there was a point when the possibility of leaving hospital with one leg was nearly 50-50.His recovery was long and painful. In May 2021, Tiger told Golf Digest that his physical therapy was more painful than anything he had experienced before. At that stage, his immediate goal was simply to walk without crutches.By December, he was back on the course for the PNC Championship in Orlando, Florida. The event marked his first competitive appearance since the accident, and he teamed up with 12-year-old Charlie. Tiger used a golf cart to move around the course, but the pair quickly showed that they could still compete.Their final round on December 19, 2021, became one of the most memorable moments of their partnership. Tiger and Charlie made 11 consecutive birdies, finishing with a round of 57 and taking second place behind John Daly and his son. It was not a tournament victory, but the performance showed how much Tiger had achieved in just 10 months.More importantly, he was able to share that return with Charlie. After spending months working to walk again, he was back on a golf course with his son, enjoying a competition together.What did Charlie Woods say about having Tiger Woods as his caddie?Tiger’s role in Charlie’s golf career has not been limited to watching from the sidelines. He has also taken his son’s golf bag and caddied for him at junior tournaments, giving Charlie advice while allowing him to make his own decisions.One such moment came in September 2023, when Tiger caddied for Charlie at a Notah Begay III Junior Golf National Championship qualifier in Florida. Charlie won the boys’ 14-15 division after shooting rounds of 71 and 66, with his father alongside him.Speaking about the experience, Charlie explained how comfortable their relationship was during competition.“We just stay in our own little world,” Charlie said. “We take it one shot at a time. He puts me in my place. I’ll talk about the next tee shot, and he’s like, ‘No. This is the shot we’re going to focus on. Focus up. This is what we’re gonna do.’”The comment offered a glimpse into how Tiger guides his son. Instead of allowing Charlie to worry about what might happen later in a round, he brings his attention back to the shot in front of him. It is a lesson that comes from years of playing under pressure, but Tiger delivers it as a father and caddie rather than as a champion expecting his son to follow every instruction.The responsibility also meant something different for Tiger. After the 2021 crash and further problems with his right ankle, walking across a golf course was not always easy. Yet he continued to turn up for Charlie’s events and take part in the work that comes with being on his bag.How have Tiger Woods and Elin Nordegren supported Charlie Woods’ future?As Charlie moved through junior golf, his results began attracting attention beyond his family. In November 2023, he helped The Benjamin School win the Florida High School Athletic Association Class 1A state golf championship. It was a major achievement for the team, and Tiger was there to watch his son celebrate.The attention surrounding Charlie has not always been easy. Large crowds have followed him at tournaments, and his performances have often been compared with those of his father. His appearance at a PGA Tour qualifying event in February 2024 also brought intense public attention, even though he did not advance.Through these moments, Tiger and Charlie’s mother, Elin Nordegren, have remained involved in supporting his development. Their presence has allowed Charlie to keep working towards his goals while dealing with the attention that comes with his family name.Another important step came on February 10, 2026, when Charlie announced his verbal commitment to play college golf at Florida State University. He is expected to join the programme in fall 2027. The decision was his own, giving him the opportunity to build a future in college golf rather than simply follow the path taken by his father, who played at Stanford.Tiger spoke about being part of the decision-making process at the 2025 Hero World Challenge. “It’s fun to be a part of the process with Charlie and go through it and see where the opportunities that he has that he has created for himself by playing better, places that he could play, wants to play and ultimately we’ll decide where he wants to go play,” he said.Charlie reached another important milestone on November 6, 2026, when his Florida State commitment became official at a signing ceremony at The Benjamin School. Tiger and Elin were both present, sharing the moment with their son.For Tiger, it was another opportunity to watch Charlie take a step forward on his own. He was not the player making the decision or competing for a trophy. He was the father standing beside his son as he prepared for the next stage of his life.The difference between Tiger’s early years under Earl and his own approach to Charlie is clear. He has given his son the chance to enjoy golf, make choices and build a career at his own pace. His achievements on the course remain part of sporting history, but his relationship with Charlie shows another side of his life: one in which being present matters more than being in the spotlight.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Connor Hellebuyck Booed Heavily by Jets Fans on Video in Return to Winnipeg After Devils Trade
articles.summary: New Jersey Devils goaltender Connor Hellebuyck received plenty of boos from Winnipeg Jets fans at Canada Life Centre ahead of a matchup between the two teams on Tuesday.
articles.body:
New Jersey Devils goaltender Connor Hellebuyck received plenty of boos from Winnipeg Jets fans at Canada Life Centre ahead of a matchup between the two teams on Tuesday.

Hellebuyck was traded from the Jets to the Devils on Oct. 23 after requesting to be moved.

Hellebuyck reflected on his trade request when speaking to reporters prior to Tuesday's game.

"I will say, with all the uncertainty I was experiencing, there was some moments and some things that happened to my family that, for me, crossed the line," Hellebuyck said. "And as a husband and a father, I felt made that decision very certain."

The 33-year-old spent the first 11 seasons of his NHL career in Winnipeg from 2015-26.

Hellebuyck blossomed into a star on the Jets, becoming a three-time Vezina Trophy winner while capturing the Hart Memorial Trophy as the league's most valuable player to his team for his 2024-25 campaign.

His production declined throughout the 2025-26 season, posting a career-low .895 save percentage in 57 appearances.

Hellebuyck eventually requested a trade from Winnipeg during the ensuing offseason and was suspended by the team after refusing to report to training camp this year.

He was eventually dealt to the Devils in exchange for Dawson Mercer, Nick Bjugstad, Nico Daws, Alexander Command, a 2027 seventh-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick.

Hellebuyck has suited up in five games for New Jersey this season, recording 105 saves on 115 shots while compiling a 5-0 record.

He appeared to be set to start Tuesday's game against his former team, although Devils general manager Sunny Mehta said that the decision was made to play Jake Allen over Hellebuyck due to a potential "reduction in our expected win probability" as part of a statement released Sunday.

Jets coach Scott Arniel was disappointed in New Jersey's decision.

"I've seen a lot of analytics in my life. I'm not sure how this works into the analytics part of it," Arniel said, per ESPN's Greg Wyshynski . "I know it's their decision. They can do whatever they want. But that would put closure to it. This doesn't."

The Devils own a 13-5-0 record to open the year, while the Jets sit at 7-8-3.

articles.title: SEC head Greg Sankey blasts announcers for criticizing poor officiating in Texas-Missouri: 'Unacceptable'
articles.summary: Greg Sankey attacked announcers for criticizing SEC officiating after the Texas Longhorns-Missouri Tigers game, drawing a rebuke from Terry McAuley.
articles.body: For most neutral fans and viewers watching Saturday's game between the Texas Longhorns and Missouri Tigers, there was a clear and obvious issue with the officiating. A number of calls were either seemingly mishandled, called incorrectly or slanted in favor of one side or the other. More often than not, in the Longhorns' direction. To the point where the announcers covering the game, Joe Tessitore and Jesse Palmer, commented on it. Palmer at one point during the game was very forthcoming, saying he'd be furious if he were a Missouri fan. MIAMI COACH FURIOUS WITH OFFICIALS AFTER POSSIBLE TD CATCH RULED INCOMPLETE IN CRUCIAL LOSS TO NOTRE DAME "I’m just going to say this. No skin in the game, [but] if you’re a Missouri fan, if you’re Eli Drinkwitz, you are livid," he said. "Because it does feel like a lot of these calls are going against Missouri today." He said it again later, in the fourth quarter. The refs missed a key penalty when a Texas defender forcibly knocked over a Missouri wide receiver away from the play, which should have resulted in an unnecessary roughness penalty and a free first down and 15-yards. Instead, no call, and Palmer was once again flabbergasted. REFS' CRUCIAL NO CALL LOOMS LARGE OVER GEORGIA'S VICTORY OVER ALABAMA "I can’t believe I’m saying this ... but I think on that last play, this reffing crew missed another call that negatively impacts Missouri," he said. One of the most obvious and controversial calls was the "fumble" from Texas QB Arch Manning on a third down play in the third quarter. Manning's arm appeared to be coming forward as the ball left his hand, which would have made the play an incomplete pass and forced a tough decision from Texas coach Steve Sarkisian. Instead, it was ruled a fumble, with a clear recovery from the Longhorns, resulting in a pick-up of 14-yards and a first down. They went down and scored immediately afterward, helping jumpstart the win. That call drew immense criticism from all corners of the college football world, especially for how it impacted the outcome of the game. Missouri coach Eli Drinkwitz was, as Palmer suggested, livid: "If I say what I want to say, I'm going to get fined until I don't have any retirement, and I'm not going to do that. I'm not going to blame the officials. That would be disrespectful to Coach Sarkisian and his team," he said. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Well, SEC commissioner Greg Sankey clearly heard those complaints and instead of addressing the referees and their calls, he chose to ... attack the announcers. BIG 12 CONFERENCE ADMITS OFFICIALS GOT CALL WRONG THAT BENEFITED BYU COUGARS IN WIN OVER ARIZONA STATE "I am highly disappointed in announcers and their criticism, and they're wrong," he said on "The Paul Finebaum Show." "Some of the worst officials in America are those in the announcers booth. "We have officiating experts, who I turned on a game on Saturday, who was just flat wrong," he continued. "And what that creates is this narrative that we've done something wrong and that is unacceptable to me, and we have to address that." Remember, the officiating in that game was so controversial that the Missouri athletic director, Laird Veatch, published an open letter asking for more transparency from the SEC. Sankey choosing to go after the announcers instead though, is par for the course. Officiating expert and NBC rules analyst Terry McAuley saw Sankey's interview, and took the time to respond to it in a post on X. STAY "FEARLESS" ON THE GO! TAKE TOMI LAHREN WITH YOU. DOWNLOAD THE TLIF PODCAST NOW! "Football announcers in both college and the NFL in today's world are far more knowledgeable about rules than they have ever been in my lifetime. They are also more supportive of officiating than they have ever been. The three announcing crews I regularly work with are incredibly strong on their knowledge of the rules, which (fortunately?) minimizes the times I need to speak. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER Sometimes the rules get very complex and announcers do get it wrong, but sometimes the officials, including Replay, get it wrong and announcers are obliged to point it out, especially when rules are involved rather than real-time judgments. Judgments are always open for debate, but as I said, today's announcers are very deferential to judgments by officials and almost always extremely fair. If Commissioner Sankey and the SEC believe announcers are treating SEC officiating unfairly, I would suggest reaching out and working with their broadcast partners on rules/officiating would be far more effective than a broadside attack such as this." OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD That's the actual answer. Announcers rarely attack the officiating, unless they believe it's so egregious that it requires addressing. That's what happened here. It doesn't mean there's some deep-seated conspiracy on the part of the SEC to protect Texas; these types of missed calls generally even out over time and the crews could have just made a series of mistakes through sheer happenstance. Some Longhorns fans were also up in arms about calls that they believe should have gone against Missouri. But acting like the announcers are the problem, not the refs, is gaslighting. Sankey does a lot of that, normally when campaigning to get all 16 SEC teams in the 12-team College Football Playoff, but it doesn't make it any less acceptable when it's directed not just at the announcers, but everyone watching too.

articles.title: Roman Josi Chasing History as Predators Head to California
articles.summary: The Nashville Predators are kicking off their west coast road trip tonight, as they visit the Los Angeles Kings. As the trip begins, Predators captain Roman...
articles.body:
The Nashville Predators are kicking off their west coast road trip tonight, as they visit the Los Angeles Kings. As the trip begins, Predators captain Roman Josi is on the verge of making history, not just for the Predators, but also for his country.

No Swiss-born player has ever scored 800 points in the NHL. At the same time, no player has ever recorded 800 points while a member of the Predators organization. Josi has the opportunity to do both with his next point, as he currently sits on 799 in his career.

The odds of Josi accomplishing the impressive feat tonight seem very high. He's entering the road trip with five points in his last three games, including a two-point performance in his last outing against the St. Louis Blues.

Josi is one of just two Swiss players to play more than 1,000 games, along with current Winnipeg Jets forward Nino Neiderreiter. He's also the only player in franchise history to play 1,000 or more games with the Predators organization.

Roman Josi is going to be remembered as a key piece of both the Nashville Predators organization and Swiss hockey for a long time to come, now we just have to see how much more history he has left to make.

articles.title: Mariners not expected to bring J.P. Crawford back; players react to Crawford’s impact
articles.summary: Longest-tenured Mariner not expected to return to club; Julio Rodriguez, Cal Raleigh, Cole Young and Bryan Woo on J.P. Crawford’s impact
articles.body:
As the off-season moves on and the 2027 Mariners roster takes shape, it will apparently be lacking the longest-tenured Mariner. Adam Jude of the Seattle Times reports that the Mariners have informed J.P. Crawford the team doesn't intend to bring back the 32-year-old shortstop, who just completed the final year of a five-year contract extension. He's been a Mariner since 2019, the longest-tenured player in the clubhouse since Dylan Moore departed in 2025.

At the end of the 2026 season, Cal Raleigh talked about how seeing Mitch Haniger's go-ahead single from Game 161 in 2021 in a video package on the big board reminded him of his first year in the big leagues, coming up and watching Crawford who was in the midst of what was at the time his best career season.

"J.P.'s been here the entire time I've been in this organization…he's been a great person, a great leader, a great staple in this clubhouse. It's been a pleasure being his teammate."

"I love J.P. the player, I love the person. It was a little emotional seeing him walk off the field, not knowing what's going to happen. It's just tough. You spend so much time with these people, you invest yourself and your livelihood with them…it's just hard. It's hard turning that page."

Assuming this is the end, Crawford's 974 games rank as 10th most in team history. Crawford's final game as a Mariner was marked by a long and loud standing ovation after he was removed from the final game of the season in the fifth inning.

"The ovation, the love that he got, there's a reason for it," said Bryan Woo. "He means to much to the team, the organization, the fans, everybody. He was a huge piece in the turnaround of this organization and so he got recognized for that."

After arriving in 2019 in a major trade with the Phillies, Crawford was the face of the youth movement in the Mariners under Jerry Dipoto, memorably present for the passing of the torch at both Félix Hernández's final game as a Mariner and Kyle Seager's. 2019-2021 were turbulent years for the growing-pains Mariners, churning through players as Dipoto sought to overhaul an aging and expensive team, but Crawford was a steady hand, anchoring the team at shortstop, and taking home a Gold Glove in 2020.

Over his eight years in Seattle, Crawford grew into a clubhouse leader, establishing relationships with every player regardless of position or level. After signing his contract extension, he purchased a home in Woodinville that is the de facto gathering space for team parties, like the annual "Crawchella" he hosts.

"That's my brother, man," said Julio Rodríguez at the end of the season.

"Like, even before I got to the big league club I got to play with him and actually, we got tight. We always had a great relationship before, but after I started playing with him, he became my brother. We're always gonna be brothers. Baseball is one thing, but the person he's shown me that he is, that's a special person, and that's the least I can say here in front of the cameras. But I love him and I wish him the best. He's my boy."

Even as the Mariners drafted and developed Crawford's eventual replacements – shortstop Colt Emerson and Cole Young, who slid over to second base – Crawford poured energy into the younger players. He batted away questions at spring training about whether it was strained or uncomfortable to play with his own replacements, saying he was a decent person doing what a decent person does in mentoring the younger players.

Crawford developed an especially close relationship with Young, who he played with for two seasons, although Young says their relationship started even earlier than that.

"He's been awesome to me," said Young. "I'm not saying just saying that to say it. Even since day one of big-league spring training camp when I was still in A ball, he was always friendly towards me – I guess knew I would be up one day – and he became a friend when I was 19 years old. So that was the first thing I saw, how humble he is and how much he cared about the organization.

And then once I got called up, he's been a great mentor. Every day he holds me accountable to be the player I can be and the person I can be. And he's been a really good friend, too. It's funny because every time in the infield if I'll say something negative, he'll find a way to switch it back and make it positive. It just shows how much he cares about his teammates."

The shape of the Mariners clubhouse – which consistently draws praise from players who arrive via trades or waiver claims – has undoubtedly been strongly influenced by the personality of the California-born, reggae-loving, come-as-you-are Crawford, whose example empowered other players to be themselves.

"Since I got here, I feel like he's always had my back, and that's something I want to continue to carry for the people that come here," said Julio. "Some people want to put others in a box, but we're all different. We all come from different places. And there are some people that don't get that, and try to push whatever they want onto somebody else. But he definitely represents being who you are, representing where you come from, and that's – I can say that about myself, too. Whoever you want to be, just make sure you're aligned with us, and that's fine."

Appreciating people's differences while making a unified whole is what Young says he's learned from Crawford and what he plans to do going forward.

"I'll come to the field every day and go about my business and do all my routines and play the game hard but I'll also be a friendly person," Young said. "I'll take the time to get to know someone and be friends with them. Talk through every situation. Be friendly and open. Everyone approaches the game differently, and everyone is a different person, and just having that open mindset of like, okay, this person's this way, just being open to everyone and friendly to everyone. That's so important. In baseball you meet so many different people from so many different backgrounds. It's so important to be open-minded and get close to your teammates and have a good vibe, especially on the field and in the clubhouse, be friends with them."

The separator for Crawford, his teammates say, is the genuine care he shows for his teammates, on and off the field.

"I think it's a different outlook than most people," said Young. "Like it's more person-based, which is very unique. A lot of people just look at the numbers, all that stuff. But I think J.P. just really cares about the person in the clubhouse. I'm not just saying that.

The way that J.P. has interacted with me, he's just a good friend. Not just someone you come to the field with and see them for whenever you're on the field and then never talk to them after that. He's an actual friend. And when you come to the field and have that – especially when you first get called up – you feel more welcome. You feel like you have someone in your corner."

Now Young and his teammates will have to move on without J.P. in their corner – literally, there will be a notable absence in the clubhouse where Crawford's locker (and nearby lockers that occasionally get annexed) has been a fixture for the past eight years. But Young will take the lessons he learned from Crawford – about including younger players from the jump rather than hazing them, showing genuine care and friendship for teammates, and treating everyone equally while also letting them be themselves – into the next iteration of the Mariners clubhouse.

"Yeah, you carry the speaker because you're a rookie, but it's just fun. It's fun stuff," said Young. "He's just always been a good friend. There are a lot of things I'll take from him, but that's one of the biggest takeaways. No matter who you are, how established you are, he'll treat you the same and show you respect, and even if you're not established at all, he's still going to be friends with you. It just shows how good of a person he is.

That's what I learned from J.P., how important it is to know your teammates and be a good person. That's what I'm going to do, lead by example, the same way that he did."

articles.title: New York Yankees Announce Giancarlo Stanton News During GM Meetings
articles.summary: New York Yankees general manager Brian Cashman announced Giancarlo Stanton news during the 2026 GM Meetings. The post New York Yankees Announce Giancarlo Sta...
articles.body:
Many believe that it's time for the New York Yankees to move on from Giancarlo Stanton. He is often injured, appearing in just 24 regular-season games this year, and is under team control for only one more season.

Not to mention, the Yankees don't really have room for Stanton, a primary designated hitter at this point in his career, to play regularly unless they convert star DH Ben Rice to a full-time first baseman.

However, Yankees general manager Brian Cashman recently revealed that Stanton isn't going anywhere, at least for now.

Giancarlo Stanton Will be With New York Yankees at Spring Training

"He's not going anywhere. He'll be in spring training with us, without a doubt."

Brian Cashman says that Giancarlo Stanton will be in spring training with the Yankees next year

Looking at Giancarlo Stanton's 2026 Season

The Yankees placed Stanton on the injured list on April 28 with a right calf strain.

After suffering a left calf strain while attempting a return, Stanton was finally activated for the postseason.

The Yankees used Stanton as a pinch hitter in the playoffs. He struck out in two plate appearances against the Tampa Bay Rays in the American League Division Series.

Before being placed on the IL in April, Stanton slashed .256/.302/.422 with three home runs and 14 RBI over 24 games.

The Florida Marlins selected Stanton in the second round of the 2007 MLB Draft out of Notre Dame High School in Sherman Oaks, Calif.

Stanton made his MLB debut with the Marlins in 2010. Miami signed the slugger to a 13-year, $325 million contract extension in the 2014-15 offseason.

The Marlins traded Stanton to the Yankees after he won the National League MVP in 2017.

Over his 17-year career, Stanton has posted 47.0 bWAR and an .871 OPS with 456 home runs and 1,183 RBI. He is a five-time All-Star and two-time Silver Slugger.

articles.title: Los Angeles Lakers Cut Ties With 7-Footer Before Bucks Game
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers are reportedly parting ways with a 7-foot center less than two weeks after signing him, opening another spot on their two-way roster....
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers are making another roster change ahead of their Wednesday, Nov. 11, matchup with the Milwaukee Bucks, reportedly parting ways with a center they signed less than two weeks ago.

According to Michael Scotto of HoopsHype, the Lakers are waiving 7-foot center Lawson Lovering, ending his brief stint with the organization after signing him to a two-way contract on Oct. 28.

The move comes just 13 days after Los Angeles added Lovering, who previously spent time with the Memphis Grizzlies.

Lovering appeared in two games for the Lakers, totaling just two minutes. He did not score and recorded one rebound.

The decision is somewhat surprising considering the Lakers' recent efforts to bolster their frontcourt depth, although Lovering had not established a meaningful role in head coach JJ Redick's rotation.

Los Angeles enters Wednesday's matchup with Milwaukee at 10-2, riding a six-game winning streak.

Lakers Waive Lawson Lovering After Signing 2-Year Contract

The Lakers announced Lovering's signing on Oct. 28 , waiving forward AK Okereke to create room for the former Utah standout.

At the time, the transaction appeared to give Los Angeles additional developmental depth at center.

Lovering, 23, appeared in 30 games for the Memphis Hustle in the G League last season, making 26 starts. He averaged 7.7 points, 7.1 rebounds, 1.3 assists and 1.3 blocks while shooting 59.2% from the floor.

He also appeared in two NBA games for the Grizzlies, averaging 7.0 points and 7.5 rebounds.

What's particularly notable about Tuesday's reported decision is the contract Lovering received when he joined Los Angeles.

As Heavy's Matt Evans previously reported , Lovering signed a two-year, two-way deal rather than the more conventional one-year arrangement.

The agreement initially suggested the Lakers were interested in a longer-term developmental project.

Instead, Lovering is reportedly headed back to the open market before completing his first full month with the franchise.

His departure also represents another quick reversal involving the Lakers' developmental roster. Los Angeles waived Okereke to sign Lovering, only to reportedly move on from his replacement less than two weeks later.

Lakers Roster Move Opens Two-Way Spot Before Bucks Game

The decision to waive Lovering would open a two-way roster spot for the Lakers, potentially allowing the front office to pursue another developmental prospect.

Under NBA rules, teams can carry up to three players on two-way contracts in addition to their standard roster.

With Lovering departing, forward Arthur Kaluma and guard Chris Mañon would remain as the Lakers' two-way players.

The move does not necessarily signal an immediate addition, however. Scotto's report did not identify a replacement or explain why the Lakers decided to release Lovering so quickly.

Los Angeles also has established frontcourt options in Walker Kessler, Kevon Looney and Sandro Mamukelashvili, limiting the immediate need for an inexperienced center in the rotation.

Kessler is coming off a 21-point, 10-rebound performance in Monday's 124-114 victory over the Atlanta Hawks , while Mamukelashvili contributed 23 points.

Luka Doncic added 32 points, eight rebounds and 10 assists in the victory.

The Lakers will face the Bucks at Fiserv Forum on Wednesday at 8 p.m. ET, looking to extend their winning streak to seven games.

Whether Los Angeles fills Lovering's roster spot immediately or keeps it available for another opportunity is the next question for the front office.

articles.title: Jaylen Brown Gives Jayson Tatum Cold Shoulder Before Celtics vs. 76ers Tips Off
articles.summary: Brown completely ignored Tatum before the start of Tuesday night's game between the Celtics and 76ers.
articles.body:
Last month, Celtics star Jayson Tatum declared that there was "no beef" between him and Jaylen Brown, who was sent from Boston to Philadelphia during the offseason. Brown agreed, but he noted that there might be "a little lamb chops and some gravy."

Well, it appears that Brown ordered his lamb chops with extra spice.

Before the start of Tuesday night's game between the Celtics and 76ers, Tatum reached out to either shake Brown's hand or give him a quick hug, and Brown completely ignored him. NBC play-by-play announcer Noah Eagle said that Tatum and Brown also did not interact while warming up.

Tatum then shared a moment with LeBron James, who played alongside Tatum as a member of Team USA at the Paris Olympics.

The awkward moment didn't seem to impact Tatum, as he scored 11 points on 4-of-7 shooting from the field in the first quarter. Brown, meanwhile, finished the opening frame with four points and two steals, but he did pick up two fouls.

articles.title: How Holland Christian volleyball came up big in the key moments to reach regional final
articles.summary: The Maroons are headed to the regional final after besting Edwardsburg in four sets.
articles.body:
Zeeland East hosts Holland Christian in girls volleyball

The Holland Christian volleyball team came up big in big moments and is headed to the regional final.

The Maroons defeated Edwardsburg 22-25, 28-26, 26-24, 25-20 in the Division 2 regional semifinals on Tuesday, Nov. 10, at Plainwell.

After losing the first set, the Maroons won the next two in extra points to advance.

Addi Meiste led Holland Christian with 18 kills and 11 digs. Tessa Leeuw totaled 17 kills and nine digs, while Allison Lamer had 17 kills and six digs.

Setter Ella Terpstra dished out 50 assists.

The Maroons will face the Plainwell-Grand Rapids Christian winner in the Division 2 regional final at 6 p.m. Thursday, Nov. 12, at Plainwell High School.

articles.title: NMCA battles back, but falls short to Atlanta in MHSAA D4 regionals
articles.summary: A sensational volleyball season for Burt Lake NMCA ended in an MHSAA Division 4 regional semifinal loss to Atlanta in Rogers City on Tuesday.
articles.body:
ROGERS CITY — It's been a historic season for Burt Lake Northern Michigan Christian Academy volleyball .

In addition to a 20-plus win fall, the Eagles captured the program's first-ever district crown last week .

But unfortunately for the Eagles, they simply ran into one of Northern Michigan's best Division 4 programs over the last few years. And while NMCA gave that opponent a battle, the Atlanta Huskies were simply too much.

The Eagles saw their season end in a 3-1 loss to the Huskies (28-30, 13-25, 25-18, 18-25) in an MHSAA Division 4 regional semifinal at Rogers City on Tuesday, Nov. 10.

Here's some takeaways from Tuesday's regional clash.

Lengthy first-set win gives advantage to Atlanta

The opening set felt like a marathon, but even though the Eagles (24-7-2) trailed for much of it — including a 19-15 deficit after a 4-0 Atlanta run — they scrapped their way back and took the lead with a kill from freshman Lauren Ferraiuolo, which gave NMCA a 21-20 lead.

After that, it was back and forth the rest of the way, as the Eagles gave themselves multiple chances to win the set but couldn't manufacture the winning point, while the Huskies (36-1-1) hung around long enough to earn a hard-fought 30th point and take a one-set lead. Momentum was seized by Atlanta, which came out firing and built a commanding lead in the second with ferocious attacking and quality defense.

As a result, the Huskies led by two sets and looked poised to secure the sweep.

But just as it looked like it was going to be a short night for NMCA, the Eagles rallied back behind their two outside hitters, sisters Shanna and Lauren Ferraiuolo, whose attacking helped NMCA build a 20-15 lead.

As strong as those two attackers were, the superb defense by Isabel Hoffmeyer and Harper Nelund, as well as the setting of Hazel Bowman, kept the Eagles alive with a third-set victory.

Despite falling into a 6-2 hole early in the fourth, the Atlanta attackers found their groove, and it resulted in a 10-3 run that gave the Huskies a 12-9 lead. From there, Atlanta's attack overwhelmed the Eagles late.

The Huskies eventually ended the match in four sets and sent themselves to a third consecutive regional final, which will be played at 6 p.m. on Thursday, Nov. 12, in Pellston.

It was a disappointing way to go out, but the Eagles have plenty to be proud of as they delivered their greatest season in program history behind a cohesive group that won a lot and held its own against quality opponents all season.

NMCA's lone senior who played her final match was Bowman, who joined the program this summer. At the setter spot, Bowman's play was pivotal in the Eagles earning a district title.

While the Eagles won't have Bowman next season, they should be very strong again as they return Shanna and Lauren Ferraiuolo as well as Hoffmeyer and Nelund, players who were highly impactful in 2026.
